great-lakes.water_system: Great Lakes is not an incorporated municipality — it is the Naval Station Great Lakes census-designated place (ZIP 60088). Water is supplied by the U.S. Navy's own system, "Great Lakes Naval Training Station" / Naval Station Great Lakes Water Plant (IEPA system IL0975227), surface water from Lake Michigan treated at the base's own plant, serving about 23,000 people through 1,140 service connections (all classified commercial/business in IEPA records). North Chicago's system (IL0971250) is listed only as an emergency backup interconnect. There is no village water department or private utility (Aqua/Illinois American) serving this area.
great-lakes.cost_coverage: not published — the Navy's 2024 Annual Drinking Water Quality Report (IL#0975227) says nothing about lead service line replacement or who pays; its only service-line language is the standard EPA notice: "Lead in drinking water is primarily from materials and components associated with service lines and home plumbing. We cannot control the variety of materials used in plumbing components."
great-lakes.homeowner_cost: not published (not applicable in the usual sense — housing on the installation is Navy/privatized military housing, not homeowner-owned service lines)
great-lakes.how_to_check_line: not published. The IEPA Drinking Water Watch page for IL0975227 contains no service line material data, and IEPA's lead service line information page offers no public statewide inventory portal — it directs residents to contact their water supply directly or IEPA at EPA.LeadandCopper@illinois.gov / (217) 785-0561. For this system the published contacts are the base Water Supervisor (847) 688-2121 x137 or Utilities Director x130.
great-lakes.how_to_apply: not published — no replacement program exists per official pages; questions go to NAVFAC Public Works Department / Naval Station Great Lakes Water Plant, Water Supervisor (847) 688-2121 x137
great-lakes.notes: Official Navy CCR (reporting year 2023) states the system is "fully compliant with all State / Federal regulations governing the control of lead and copper"; lead 90th percentile at consumer taps was <1.0 ppb (action level 15 ppb), copper 0.26 ppm — well under action levels. The base remains under an Agreement on Consent with US EPA over aging treatment-plant infrastructure (a Nov 1, 2022 Notice of Violation for structural deterioration and low flow in the clearwell tank; new clearwell tanks are being designed) — this concerns the treatment plant, not lead service lines. CNIC also maintains a "Lead in Priority Area Sampling Program – NAVSTA Great Lakes" page (cnrma.cnic.navy.mil), but the page body could not be retrieved (site blocks automated access; archived copy contains only navigation). Because this is a federal DoD-owned water system, the Illinois municipal-style village cost-share programs do not apply here; the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act inventory requirements are administered through IEPA, and no inventory data for IL0975227 is published on Drinking Water Watch.

green-oaks.water_system: Village of Green Oaks operates its own small community water system (Public Water System ID IL0970040) as purchased surface water — the 2025 CCR states "Waukegan is the Source of Green Oaks Water" (Lake Michigan water bought wholesale from the City of Waukegan; single metered connection at O'Plaine Rd and Dan Patch Ln). The system is small (~479 service lines in the inventory) and much of the village is on private wells/septic — connection to village water is only required if a well fails. Day-to-day water operations are handled by the village's engineering firm, Gewalt Hamilton Associates (water operator Jason DesBiens, 847-821-6207).
green-oaks.cost_coverage: not published — no lead service line replacement program or cost-sharing policy appears anywhere on greenoaks.org or in the 2025 CCR. Notably, the village's posted IEPA Lead Service Line Inventory (479 service lines) records ZERO lead lines and zero galvanized-requiring-replacement lines: all utility-side lines are copper (476) or cast/ductile iron (3); 431 lines classified Non-Lead, ~47 with customer-side material still blank/unverified. With no lead lines identified, there is nothing published to replace.
green-oaks.how_to_check_line: The village posts its IEPA lead service line material inventory spreadsheet (address-by-address) on the Engineering page of greenoaks.org. Per the CCR, residents can obtain a copy of the service line inventory and lead tap sampling data by emailing Jason DesBiens at jdesbiens@gha-engineers.com. The village's IEPA public notice tells residents: "Learn what your service line material is. Contact us at leadtesting@greenoaks.org or a licensed plumber," and points to EPA's Protect Your Tap guide (www.epa.gov/pyt).
green-oaks.how_to_apply: not published — no application process exists since no replacement program is published. Water/lead questions: leadtesting@greenoaks.org (include phone number for a callback), water operator Jason DesBiens 847-821-6207 (jdesbiens@gha-engineers.com, Gewalt Hamilton Associates), or Village Hall (847) 362-5363.
green-oaks.notes: Compliance history is the main story: the 2025 CCR's violations table shows Green Oaks failed to develop and submit its initial service line inventory to Illinois EPA by the October 16, 2024 deadline (LSL INVENTORY-INITIAL and LSL REPORTING-INITIAL violations), failed the known/potential-LSL consumer notification certification (07/02/2025), and had a linked public-notice violation (08/22/2025–01/12/2026). The village mailed an IEPA public notice to customers on January 12, 2026 stating: "the Village of Green Oaks is preparing a lead service line inventory and plans to submit the inventory to the IEPA in Winter, 2026. Customers will be notified should they be impacted by an identified lead service line via mail." The CCR adds the inventory work has "less than 20 homes remaining." The now-posted inventory (filename dated 2026-04-20) shows 479 lines, 0 lead, 0 GRR — a fairly new system (homes mostly 1980s-2000s per install years), so lead lines are unlikely. Lead 90th percentile was 5 ug/L (Aug 2023 sampling), well under the 15 ug/L action level. Residents on private wells are outside this system entirely. Corrosion control: 60/40 poly/ortho phosphate blend treated at Waukegan's source.

gurnee.water_system: Village of Gurnee operates its own distribution system (over 9,800 water accounts, 188+ miles of water main) and purchases Lake Michigan water treated by the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA) in Lake Bluff; two emergency backup wells plus a backup connection to the City of Waukegan.
gurnee.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's 2025 Water Quality Report states verbatim: "The Village of Gurnee water supply has developed a service line material inventory. There are no known lead or galvanized service lines in the Village of Gurnee." With no known lead lines, the official pages describe no replacement program or cost-sharing terms. The report also states generally: "The Village of Gurnee is responsible for providing high quality drinking water and removing lead pipes, but cannot control the variety of materials used in the plumbing in your home."
gurnee.how_to_check_line: Official Water Service Line Inventory map (ArcGIS) linked from www.gurnee.il.us/waterservice — "The inventory contains the known materials that make up the private and public water service lines in our water system." Or request a copy of the inventory from Brett Fritzler, Gurnee Public Works, (847) 599-6800 / brettf@village.gurnee.il.us.
gurnee.how_to_apply: not published (no replacement program exists to apply to). For lead concerns or water testing: Village of Gurnee at 847-599-6800; lead tap sampling data via Brett Fritzler, (847) 599-6800.
gurnee.notes: Gurnee is an outlier among Chicago suburbs: its LSLRNA-required inventory is complete and the Village officially reports zero known lead or galvanized service lines, so no replacement program, timeline, waitlist, or cost policy is published. 2024 lead tap sampling 90th percentile was 2.3 ppb (action level 15 ppb), 0 sites over AL, in compliance. CLCJAWA adds phosphate at treatment "to prevent metals like lead and copper from getting into the water from home plumbing." Residents concerned about lead in in-home plumbing are directed to standard precautions (ANSI-certified filters, cold-water use, flushing) and can have water tested via the Village at 847-599-6800.

harwood-heights.water_system: Harwood Heights operates its own community water supply: "The Community Water Supply (CWS) is named Harwood Heights and is IEPA Water System No. IL0311140. The CWS serves a population of 9,065 and has 2,225 service connections as reported to the IEPA." The upstream source-water supplier is not stated in the plan text (the annual water quality report PDF is scanned images and not machine-readable).
harwood-heights.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Program (per the Village's 2026 Draft Lead Service Line Replacement Plan, REL Project 22-R0903, dated April 15, 2026)
harwood-heights.cost_coverage: $0 under the Village's stated program intent — the draft plan commits to completing replacements without "requiring property owners to pay a portion of the replacement cost." However, this depends on IEPA SRF forgivable-loan funding the Village has applied for but not yet received, and program replacements proceed by prioritized census tract over several years (Census Tract 8106 first). For a full replacement requested by the property owner outside the program schedule (e.g., during emergency work), the plan notes the CWS "is not required to fund the full replacement" and that "funding terms will be discussed at the time of the work." No fee schedule is published.
harwood-heights.homeowner_cost: $0 under the Village's stated program intent — the plan commits to completing replacements without "requiring property owners to pay a portion of the replacement cost." However, for a full replacement requested by the property owner outside the program schedule, the plan notes the CWS "is not required to fund the full replacement." No fee schedule is published.
harwood-heights.how_to_check_line: The Village publishes its full address-by-address 2026 Service Line Material Inventory as a PDF on the Water Quality Reports page (harwoodheights.org/public-works/water-quality-reports/) — it lists every service address with PWS-owned and customer-side material and an entire-line classification (Lead/Non-Lead/Unknown). No interactive lookup portal exists; residents can also call Public Works at (708) 867-7206.
harwood-heights.how_to_apply: not published — no application form or sign-up process is described. The program is area-based: project areas are prioritized by census tract to maximize IEPA SRF forgivable-loan scoring, and "Notices will be sent to homeowners at least 45 days before the commencement of work." Contacts: Public Works (708) 867-7206, 7101 W. Wilson; Village office (708) 867-7200.
harwood-heights.notes: Inventory (2026 submission): 2,225 total service lines — 206 lead, 5 unknown, 0 galvanized-requiring-replacement, 2,014 non-lead. Only 5 LSLs have been replaced since 2020, so the program is essentially just starting. "Replacements will begin in Census Tract 8106. These replacements are expected to last four years at the mandated replacement rate but will depend on the maximum amount of annual IEPA SRF funding received." New lines will be copper; trenchless methods (pipe pulling) preferred; no lead piping left in the system; interior/exterior restoration to "existing condition or better." Property owners get an optional free tap-water lead test 3-6 months after replacement. Homeowners who decline access may sign an IDPH waiver — the Village "lacks the authority to mandate homeowner access to private property." Funding backups being evaluated: CDBG, DCEO grants, Congressional discretionary funding, and USEPA Community Change Grants. Ownership split: Village owns main-to-B-box/curb stop; property owner owns B-box to building. The plan is labeled "Draft" and is the Village's second annual plan. No mention of coordinating replacements with water-main projects.

hawthorn-woods.water_system: Private utility: Aqua Illinois. The Village FAQ states "Water is provided through our management partner Aqua Illinois," which manages the Village's municipal well system. The regulated system is "Aqua Illinois-Hawthorn Woods," System No. IL0975040, privately owned and operated by Aqua Illinois, sourced from two deep wells (Galesville Aquifer), serving ~3,065 people / 1,343 service connections. Areas served include Hawthorn Woods Country Club, Hawthorn Ridge, The Commons, Hawthorn Trails, Countryside Meadows, Hawthorn Hills, The Sanctuary Club, Kildeer Estates, Wentworth of Kildeer, Glenshire, Stone Bridge, Forest Lake, and Spencer Loomis Middle School.
hawthorn-woods.program_name: not named (referred to as the Aqua Illinois-Hawthorn Woods "Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Plan," April 2025 draft, per Public Act 102-0613)
hawthorn-woods.cost_coverage: Intended $0 (no direct cost to customers, recovered through statewide water rates), subject to Illinois Commerce Commission approval for the customer-owned side. Not yet a guaranteed commitment; plan estimates full replacement at ~$15,000 and single-side at ~$8,000 per line, total program $0-$45,000.
hawthorn-woods.homeowner_cost: Intended $0 (no direct cost to customers, recovered through statewide water rates), subject to Illinois Commerce Commission approval for the customer-owned side. Not yet a guaranteed commitment; plan estimates full replacement at ~$15,000 and single-side at ~$8,000 per line, total program $0-$45,000.
hawthorn-woods.how_to_check_line: Aqua Illinois publishes service line inventory tables/summaries as PDFs by division at aquawater.com (Lead Service Line Materials Inventory page); no interactive address-lookup portal is published. The plan states Aqua's website (www.aquawater.com/lead) provides information explaining how customers can identify their service line material (customer self-reporting). Questions: 1-866-SLM-AQUA (1-866-756-2782) or AquaILLead@AquaWater.com.
hawthorn-woods.how_to_apply: No application process published (no eligible lines currently identified). Contact Aqua Illinois: 1-866-756-2782 (lead line), Customer Service (877) 987-2782, or AquaILLead@AquaWater.com; LSLR plan comments via the Aqua website.
hawthorn-woods.notes: Key fact: as of March 24, 2025, the Hawthorn Woods system inventory shows 0 lead lines, 0 galvanized-requiring-replacement, 58 unknown, 1,285 non-lead out of 1,343 services; unknowns are "not expected to be lead or galvanized," so the system "may be lead, GRR, and unknown free by the final plan submittal in 2027." If any are found, Public Act 102-0613 requires replacing 7%/year starting 2027 (LCRI may raise to 10%). Replacements would occur during infrastructure work (water main replacements, leak/break repairs) and prioritized high-risk connections. Final LSLR plan and inventory due to IEPA April 15, 2027; plan updated annually. As a private utility, Aqua is ineligible for standard SRF loans but can seek BIL zero-interest loans; it will "look for grant opportunities to reduce costs for low-income Hawthorn Woods residents." The Village of Hawthorn Woods itself publishes no village-run replacement program — the Aqua Illinois plan is the applicable program. Homes on private wells are outside this system entirely.

highland-park.water_system: Own municipal system — City of Highland Park Public Works, Water Production Division (city operates its own water plant; Water Plant Division 847.433.4355)
highland-park.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement Program (City of Highland Park; program website GetTheLeadOutIL.com/highlandpark)
highland-park.cost_coverage: Public portion: the City owns the public service line ("from the water main to the water meter pit or buffalo-box (b-box) or shut-off valve within the City right-of-way") and "The City will assume the cost of work on properties that only require work on the public side service lines." Private portion (b-box/meter pit into the house): "The City has developed a cost share program... the property owner is responsible for a $5,000 cost share fee, and the City will pay the balance of the LSL replacement expense." Only properties receiving private-side replacement are charged the $5,000. The cost share is offered through the City's current LSL Replacement Program, which is rolling out by designated project areas (Project Area #1 notified February 2025; program timeline roughly February 2025 – July 2028) — replacements happen when the program reaches your area, and the City cautions there is "no guarantee that a portion of the costs will be covered again in the future" for owners who decline to participate now. Project largely financed via the IEPA Public Water Supply Loan Program / Illinois State Revolving Fund (SRF). | Homeowner cost: $5,000 flat cost-share fee if the private side is replaced ($0 if only public side needs work). Payable in full or via a City-administered payment plan/loan agreement plus a $500 administrative and processing fee. Owners qualifying for the City's Low-Income Assistance Program get a 50% reduction ($2,500); contact finance@cityhpil.com. Note: yard/structural restoration is included, but interior decorative restoration (e.g., tile or drywall) is the property owner's responsibility and is an additional cost beyond the $5,000.
highland-park.homeowner_cost: $5,000 flat cost-share fee if the private side is replaced ($0 if only public side needs work). Payable in full or via a City-administered payment plan/loan agreement plus a $500 administrative and processing fee. Owners qualifying for the City's Low-Income Assistance Program get a 50% reduction ($2,500); contact finance@cityhpil.com. Interior decorative restoration (e.g., tile or drywall) is the owner's responsibility and an additional cost beyond the $5,000. The cost share is offered as the program reaches your designated project area (rollout roughly February 2025 - July 2028), and the City cautions there is "no guarantee that a portion of the costs will be covered again in the future" for owners who decline to participate.
highland-park.how_to_check_line: City GIS Lead Service Line Map dashboard: https://highlandparkil.maps.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/e05e0e22d9914af19c79698a600f183e (linked from cityhpil.com/leadinformation). Residents can report inaccuracies via the online "Water Service Line Material" form; the program also asks owners to submit photos of their service line at GetTheLeadOutIL.com/survey.
highland-park.how_to_apply: Sign up at GetTheLeadOutIL.com/highlandpark and submit service-line photos at GetTheLeadOutIL.com/survey. Questions: City consultant Robinson Engineering 847-590-4624 / lslr@reltd.com; Public Works 847.432.0807 / publicworks@cityhpil.com; cost-share questions: Keith Miller, Utilities Superintendent, 847.926.1152 / kmiller@cityhpil.com.
highland-park.notes: Program is being rolled out by project areas (Project Area #1 notices mailed Feb 2025); overall timeline stated as February 2025 – July 2028. Participation is voluntary, but the City warns there is "no guarantee that a portion of the costs will be covered again in the future" — state law (Public Act 102-0613) requires all LSLs replaced by 2035 (city's stated deadline for its size tier). New line is copper; contractor digs two 6x6-ft holes, water off up to 4 hours, outdoor meter pits moved inside. Structural interior restoration and sod restoration included; decorative restoration (tile/drywall) is the owner's responsibility. Free water sampling offered 3-6 months post-replacement; filters provided after replacement. Robinson Engineering Ltd. designed and administers the program.

hoffman-estates.water_system: Village of Hoffman Estates operates its own distribution system; water is Lake Michigan water delivered by the Northwest Municipal Joint Action Water Agency (JAWA), sourced from the City of Chicago's water treatment plant (PWS ID# 0311290)
hoffman-estates.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's official pages state "There are no known lead service lines within the Village," so no replacement program or cost-coverage policy is described
hoffman-estates.how_to_check_line: No inventory map/portal published on the pages read. Residents concerned about lead can contact Public Works, which "offers water testing to residents concerned about lead levels" by appointment: (847) 490-6800, PublicWorks@vohe.org. Search snippets from hoffmanestates.org indicate the Village completed an inventory of all service line materials (available on request from Public Works, 2305 Pembroke Ave), but that specific page could not be fetched directly.
hoffman-estates.how_to_apply: not published (no program exists per official pages); general contact: Public Works Department, (847) 490-6800, PublicWorks@vohe.org
hoffman-estates.notes: Official Village position (both fetched pages, verbatim): "There are no known lead service lines within the Village" and "Lead is not present in Village's water supply from the City of Chicago's water treatment plant, nor is Lead in the Village's water distribution system." The Village notes lead can still be present in some homes/buildings due to internal plumbing and offers free-of-charge-unspecified water testing by appointment. The 2024 Water Quality Report PDF and a news item about the completed service-line inventory returned 404 on direct fetch; per search snippets of those hoffmanestates.org documents, the Village completed an inventory of all service line materials concluding no lead service lines exist, with inventory and lead/copper sampling records available via Public Works. No replacement program, cost-sharing, waitlist, or main-project coordination is published — consistent with a no-known-lead-lines system.

hometown.water_system: City of Hometown operates its own community water system (IEPA ID IL0311320) that purchases Lake Michigan surface water directly from the City of Chicago (seller system IL0316000) through master meters (one located at 87th & Kostner), per the city's official 2022 Consumer Confidence Report ("The source of drinking water used by HOMETOWN is Purchased Surface Water"; "Source of Water: CHICAGO"). Hometown, not Chicago or Oak Lawn, is the water supply whose lead service line obligations apply to residents.
hometown.cost_coverage: not published — no lead service line replacement program, cost-sharing policy, or inventory information appears anywhere on the City of Hometown official website (Water Supply, Water Service, Public Utilities, and Public Works pages all checked) or in its published Consumer Confidence Report
hometown.how_to_check_line: not published — no service line material inventory map, portal, or lookup is posted on the city website. The only official lead-related guidance is the CCR's standard EPA language ("If you are concerned about lead in your water, you may wish to have your water tested"); the Public Works page mentions the department provides "testing of residential water." Contact Public Works at (708) 424-7503 or hometownpublicworks@gmail.com to ask about your service line material.
hometown.how_to_apply: not published — no program or application process exists on official pages. Water/lead contact per official sources: water operator Mark Trlak, (708) 424-7503 (CCR contact); Public Works Department, 4331 Southwest Highway, Hometown, IL 60456, (708) 424-7503, hometownpublicworks@gmail.com.
hometown.notes: Hometown (pop. approx. 4,200, Cook County) is subject to the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act as owner/operator of its own community water supply, but has published no inventory, replacement plan, timeline, or cost policy on its website. Its 2022 CCR (most recent found online) shows Lead and Copper sampling from 09/23/2020 with copper 90th percentile 0.147 ppm and 0 sites over the action level; a lead 90th-percentile row was not visible in the retrieved document. Any complete service line material inventory would have been filed with Illinois EPA (statutory deadline April 15, 2024) but is not posted by the city. Residents seeking inventory or replacement information must contact City Hall / Public Works directly.

homewood.water_system: Village of Homewood owns and operates its own community water system (Public Works Department). Since September 2022 it purchases Lake Michigan water from the City of Chicago Heights (which buys from Hammond, Indiana) via a village-owned 30-inch transmission main and booster pump station in Thornton; previous supplier was the City of Harvey. The Village's own LSLR program applies.
homewood.cost_coverage: Official FAQ: "If you choose to replace your lead service line before the Village visits your street, you would be responsible for the cost which is currently estimated at $10,000 in 2024." No out-of-pocket charge is published for village-scheduled replacements; the FAQ says the program "will be funded by federal and state programs in addition to all water users within the Village of Homewood" and that water rates and fees "may also be impacted" village-wide. Private lead testing is at the resident's own cost. Under village-scheduled replacements the contract covers the full line — a new 1-inch copper line connected "to the Village's water main and to the interior plumbing of the residence or building" (Dec 9, 2025 board memo) — though access agreements outline restoration responsibilities shared between the Village and the property owner, and the official pages contain no explicit "at no cost to the homeowner" statement.
homewood.homeowner_cost: Official FAQ: "If you choose to replace your lead service line before the Village visits your street, you would be responsible for the cost which is currently estimated at $10,000 in 2024." No out-of-pocket charge is published for village-scheduled replacements; water rates and fees may be impacted village-wide. Private lead testing is also at the resident's own cost.
homewood.how_to_check_line: The Village is collecting service line material data from each household (lead vs. copper; galvanized steel also must be replaced) and completed its initial service line inventory submission to IEPA in April 2023. Official FAQ: "You will be notified by written letter via USPS if we do not currently have information on your home's water line materials." No public online inventory map/portal is published; the village says it "will have a map of homes and areas they will replace annually" and "all homes that need a lsl replacement will receive one and residents will be notified."
homewood.how_to_apply: not published — there is no application; replacement is village-scheduled by an annual prioritization map, and residents are contacted directly (notification letters, then access agreements distributed to property owners before construction). Program page is hosted under the village's government departments (Public Works Director Joshua Burman oversees the program per board records), but no enrollment form or dedicated contact is published on the program page.
homewood.notes: Scale/timeline (official Dec 9, 2025 board memo): 4,363 total lead service lines; 10-year implementation plan under Public Act 102-0613 — 267 replacements starting Spring 2026 (contract awarded to Trine Construction Corp., not to exceed $2,339,000, contingent on IEPA approval; funding source Water Sewer Capital), then 410/year 2027-2035 and 406 in 2036. Priority order per EPA Revised Lead and Copper Rule: "vulnerable populations" first (schools and childcare facilities). Method is directional boring (2-3 small pits, new 1-inch copper line pulled from street into the building, foundation penetrations sealed, pits backfilled). Replacements are scheduled area-by-area via an annual map, not driven by resident applications; the older program page text referenced a 17-year plan, but the adopted plan is 10 years (complete by 2036). The village site (village.homewood.il.us) blocks automated fetching (Akamai 403); official page content was obtained via search-index verbatim snippets of the page plus the village's own board memorandum PDF read in full. Caution: a WebFetch auto-summary of that PDF hallucinated a public/private cost split ("Village replaces public portion at no cost, homeowner pays private portion") that does NOT appear in the actual document — disregard that claim.

indian-creek.water_system: Indian Creek has no municipal water system of its own (the village, pop. ~500, has no website or public works department). It is served by Lake County Public Works (LCPW) as part of the "Vernon Hills Water Service Area (includes Herons Landing, Indian Creek, Knollwood, Rondout, South Bradley Road, Countryside Manor)" per LCPW's official Annual Water Quality Report. Water is Lake Michigan water purchased from the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA), treated at the Paul M. Neal facility.
indian-creek.program_name: not named (LCPW "Lead Service Line Replacement Plan" — a compliance plan filed with Illinois EPA, not a branded homeowner program)
indian-creek.cost_coverage: Not published as a funded program. LCPW's official pages state: "Illinois State law requires all Illinois utilities to develop and submit lead service line replacement plans. LCPW has developed this initial plan (PDF) to comply with the law and the federal Lead and Copper Rule Revision. It's being updated annually and will be resubmitted to the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency until the final plan and inventory are submitted in April 2027." The Lead FAQ states: "The public water distribution system has no lead water lines. However, homeowners may have lead lines on their property" and "If your service line has lead, the homeowner should consider replacing the service line with a different pipe material." No county-paid replacement, cost-share, or reimbursement is stated anywhere on the official pages.
indian-creek.homeowner_cost: not published (FAQ language puts replacement of privately owned lead lines on the homeowner — "the homeowner should consider replacing the service line" — but no dollar figures or cost-share terms are published)
indian-creek.how_to_check_line: Two official routes: (1) LCPW interactive Water Service Line Map showing "the locations and materials of water service lines that connect to LCPW's water system" (ArcGIS viewer linked from lakecountyil.gov/3668); (2) self-check guide at lakecountyil.gov/4817 (scratch/magnet/tapping tests for structures built 1988 or earlier), then submit results via the "Water Service Line Self-Identification Form"; residents unable to determine material can contact publicworks@lakecountyil.gov or 847-377-7500.
indian-creek.how_to_apply: not published (no application/enrollment process exists; contact Lake County Public Works at 847-377-7500 or publicworks@lakecountyil.gov; water testing available via Lake County Environmental Laboratory, 847-377-7741)
indian-creek.notes: Note: lakecountyil.gov blocks automated fetching (Cloudflare), so pages were read via Internet Archive snapshots (Feb 2026) of the official URLs listed. Key facts: LCPW says the public distribution system itself contains no lead water mains; lead risk is on private-side service lines and home plumbing. LCPW is building its service line material inventory from installation records, field inspections, and customer submissions, with final plan and inventory due to Illinois EPA in April 2027. Lead sampling in the Vernon Hills service area (which includes Indian Creek): 2023 90th percentile lead <1 ppb, 0 sites over the 15 ppb action level; LCPW adds polyphosphate for corrosion control. Unlike many Chicago-suburb villages, there is no published village- or county-funded replacement, no cost-share/loan program, and no water-main-project-driven replacement scheduling for Indian Creek. The Village of Indian Creek itself publishes nothing (no website found); LCPW is the responsible water utility under the Illinois LSLR and Notification Act.

inverness.water_system: Inverness has NO municipal water system. Per the official Village of Inverness site: "Most Inverness homes are on private wells and septic systems." Exceptions by subdivision: Inverness on the Ponds, the Shires of Inverness, Maison du Comte, Ashbury and the Enclave are served by the Village of Palatine (847-359-9082); Braymore Hills, Sanctuary II of Inverness, Glencrest III, Weatherstone and the Estates at Inverness Ridge are served by the Village of Barrington (847-304-3430).
inverness.program_name: not named (Inverness itself has none; suppliers' programs: Palatine's "Lead and Galvanized Steel Water Service Line Replacement Cost Sharing Program"; Barrington's "Lead Water Service Line Replacement" program)
inverness.cost_coverage: Inverness publishes no lead service line program of its own (per its Utility Information page, "Most Inverness homes are on private wells and septic systems"; specific subdivisions are served by the Village of Palatine or the Village of Barrington). Supplier programs per their official pages: Palatine — "the Village will reimburse 100% of the cost to replace the lead or galvanized steel service line from the water main to the water shut off valve (b-box)... and 3/4 of the cost from the b-box to the meter, up to a $11,000 maximum reimbursement" ("Participation is voluntary"). Barrington — "The Village of Barrington has secured grant funding from the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency to help cover the cost of the replacement program, which will come at no cost to any individual homeowner." Neither page states whether these programs extend to Inverness addresses on their systems. Homeowner cost: not published for Inverness itself (no program). On Palatine's system: homeowner pays 1/4 of the b-box-to-meter portion plus anything above the $11,000 reimbursement cap; permit and inspection fees are paid up front by the resident/applicant but per the Village are "eligible in addition to the reimbursement cap of $11,000" (i.e., reimbursable on top of the cap). On Barrington's system: "no cost to any individual homeowner."
inverness.homeowner_cost: not published for Inverness itself (no program). On Palatine's system: homeowner pays 1/4 of the b-box-to-meter portion plus anything above the $11,000 reimbursement cap; permit and inspection fees are paid up front by the resident/applicant but are "eligible in addition to the reimbursement cap of $11,000" (i.e., reimbursable on top of the cap). On Barrington's system: "no cost to any individual homeowner."
inverness.how_to_check_line: not published by Inverness. Palatine: online GIS water service inventory map ("lookup your address using the magnifying glass at the top right corner of the map") plus a scratch/magnet test guide at palatine.il.us/883. Barrington: "The Village has created an online inventory/map of lead and copper water service lines for all residential, commercial, and institutional properties" (structures built before 1986 may have lead).
inverness.how_to_apply: not published by Inverness. Palatine: "fill out and submit the application form prior to submitting for a building permit"; reimbursement request submitted to Public Works at publicworks@palatine.il.us (application PDF on palatine.il.us). Barrington: no application procedure published; contact Public Works at water@barrington-il.gov or (847) 304-3362.
inverness.notes: Inverness is an affluent, largely well-and-septic community with no community water supply of its own, so the Illinois LSLRNA inventory/replacement mandate does not attach to the Village — it attaches to Palatine and Barrington for the handful of Inverness subdivisions they serve, and homes on private wells are outside any LSL replacement program entirely. The inverness-il.gov site is behind a Cloudflare challenge; page text was verified via a Wayback Machine capture (March 2025) of the Utility Information page. Palatine's program requires licensed/bonded contractors working in Palatine and contractor restoration of disturbed public property; reimbursements are stated as not eligible for 1099 reporting. Barrington notes lead is not found in its source or treated water and that it adds polyphosphates for corrosion control; no timeline or waitlist published. Neither supplier page states whether out-of-village (Inverness) customers qualify — residents should confirm with the respective Public Works department.

kenilworth.water_system: Village of Kenilworth operates its own water system (Water Supply ID IL0311500, ~877 customers), but since decommissioning its own water plant in 2017 the water itself is supplied by the neighboring Village of Wilmette through an intergovernmental agreement — Kenilworth's own program applies to service lines
kenilworth.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement Cost-Sharing Program (also referenced as "Lead Water Service Line Replacement Cost Sharing Program" in its Guide and Application document)
kenilworth.cost_coverage: Village reimburses homeowners "100% of the cost to replace the lead service line from the water main to the water shut-off valve (b-box)," including pavement and parkway restoration; for the private portion the Village contributes "50% up to a $3,000 maximum reimbursement for the portion of the water service from the b-box to the water meter." This is a reimbursement (cost-sharing) program, not direct Village payment. Program effective January 1, 2027; the program budget is set annually by the Village Board and funds are distributed "on a first-come, first-served basis," so reimbursement is subject to available annual funding. Applicants must meet eligibility requirements detailed in the Village's Program Guide and Application.
kenilworth.homeowner_cost: Homeowner pays the remaining 50% of the private-side (b-box to water meter) replacement cost, plus any amount by which the Village's 50% share would exceed the $3,000 reimbursement cap; public portion (main to b-box) costs the homeowner nothing
kenilworth.how_to_check_line: GIS Consortium Community Portal (apps.gisconsortium.org/CommunityPortal, Kenilworth site) — enter your address and view "Lead Service Inventory" on the property page; discrepancies reported via the online Water Service Line Material Survey form or Village Hall (847-251-1666, info@vok.org)
kenilworth.how_to_apply: Complete the "Lead Water Service Line Replacement Cost Sharing Program Guide and Application" (linked on the Village's Lead Service Line Replacement page); program questions to Jordan Schmidt, jschmidt@vok.org; general inquiries 847-251-1666 or info@vok.org
kenilworth.notes: Cost-sharing program is not yet active — effective January 1, 2027, first-come first-served funding. Village began its service line inventory in 2018 (public survey, door-to-door visits, building records); final material inventory submitted April 2024; replacement plan updated annually by April 15 each year until the final plan due April 15, 2027. As of April 15, 2026 the Village reports 65 lead service lines replaced cumulatively, with ten project areas identified for replacement over coming years (per the Village page, these are project-area replacements the Village has been completing ahead of the cost-share program). Service line materials in the Village include copper, lead, galvanized, and plastic. Official replacement plan document: vok.org/DocumentCenter/View/6462.

kildeer.water_system: Kildeer has no municipal water utility and the Village of Kildeer website publishes nothing about water supply or lead service lines. Most public-water customers in the Kildeer area are served by the private utility Aqua Illinois via its Hawthorn Woods system (IL0975040, two deep wells in the Galesville Aquifer); the system's official LSLR plan lists served areas including 'Kildeer Estates, Wentworth of Kildeer, Glenshire, Stone Bridge, Forest Lake.' A small section of Kildeer is reported to receive water from the Village of Lake Zurich's well system (IL0970850), and other homes are on private wells.
kildeer.program_name: Aqua Illinois-Hawthorn Woods Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Plan (draft, April 2025, per Public Act 102-0613); not named as a branded village program — Kildeer itself has none
kildeer.cost_coverage: Anticipated $0 direct cost to the homeowner — Aqua Illinois's draft 2025 LSLR plan for the Hawthorn Woods water system (which serves parts of Kildeer, including Kildeer Estates and Wentworth of Kildeer) states it "anticipates" replacing the customer-owned side at "no direct cost to Hawthorn Woods customers," recovered through water rates. This is a stated goal, not a guarantee: it requires Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC) approval to use water rates for customer-side work, and the plan says it will offer full replacement at no direct cost only "when financially feasible," depending on final program costs and available grants. Utilities are not legally required to pay for the customer-owned side, and homeowners must sign a license agreement to participate; if the no-cost goal is not realized, the homeowner's cost is not published.
kildeer.homeowner_cost: Anticipated $0 direct cost to the homeowner ("no direct cost to Hawthorn Woods customers") per Aqua Illinois's draft 2025 LSLR plan — contingent on ICC approval to recover customer-side costs through water rates AND on financial feasibility (the plan offers full replacement at no direct cost only "when financially feasible," depending on final program costs and available grants); participation requires signing a license agreement granting Aqua access. If the no-cost goal is not realized, the homeowner's cost is not published.
kildeer.how_to_check_line: Aqua Illinois publishes downloadable service-line material inventory PDFs per district on its Lead Service Line Materials Inventory page (item "Aqua Illinois-Hawthorn Woods IL0975040" covers the Kildeer-area subdivisions). The plan also says Aqua's website explains how customers can self-identify their service line material. No interactive address-lookup portal is published.
kildeer.how_to_apply: Not published. No application form or sign-up process appears on official pages; replacements are utility-scheduled ("during infrastructure work, including water main replacements and leak and break repairs, and through prioritized replacements"). Aqua Illinois customer line: 877.987.2782.
kildeer.notes: The Hawthorn Woods system inventory (as of March 24, 2025) shows ZERO known lead or galvanized-requiring-replacement lines on either the Aqua-owned or customer-owned side; 58 Aqua-side and 54 customer-side services are "unknown," and staff estimate 0-5% of unknowns (0-3 lines total) could be lead. Total anticipated program cost is only $0-$45,000 (avg full replacement ~$15,000/line). Statewide, Aqua Illinois plans to replace all identified lead and galvanized lines over 10 years beginning 2027; the Hawthorn Woods final plan/inventory is due to IEPA by April 15, 2027, with 7% annual replacement thereafter. Practical takeaway per official sources: lead service lines are essentially a non-issue in Kildeer's Aqua-served areas. For the small Lake Zurich-served section, Lake Zurich maintains an IEPA material inventory (dated 5/12/2025) on lakezurich.org and has bid a 2026-2027 Lead Service Line Replacement Project; its detailed cost policy was not fetched. Homes on private wells are outside any LSLR program. The Village of Kildeer itself publishes no lead service line information.

lake-barrington.water_system: No village-wide municipal water system. Per Illinois EPA Drinking Water Watch (official): (1) Village of Lake Barrington operates a small community groundwater system, "LAKE BARRINGTON" IL0971080 — 2 wells, ~500 population, 89 connections, emergency interconnect with Village of Fox River Grove; village's own site (indexed snippets) ties this system to the Lake Barrington Industrial Park ("Lake Barrington Industrial Park Annual Water Quality Report... water delivered by Village of Lake Barrington"). (2) "LAKE BARRINGTON SHORES SUBDIVSION" IL0975520 is a separate community groundwater system (~2,300 population, 256 connections) with contacts at FirstService Residential (HOA-managed), not the village. (3) Most other residents are on private wells and septic — the village website has a "Well and Septic" page directing well matters to the Lake County Health Department.
lake-barrington.how_to_check_line: not published (no Lake Barrington inventory map/portal found; Illinois EPA's lead service line page offers no resident lookup tool and directs residents to contact their water utility — for the village system, Village of Lake Barrington, 23860 N. Old Barrington Rd., 847-381-6010/847-842-6080 per IEPA contact records; for Lake Barrington Shores, the subdivision's public works via FirstService Residential, 847-382-1660)
lake-barrington.notes: IMPORTANT: nearly all "Lake Barrington lead service line" search results are for the separate Village of Barrington (barrington-il.gov), a different municipality — do not conflate. lakebarrington.org is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched by any method (WebFetch 403, curl 403 "Just a moment...", Bright Data empty), so no village lead-service-line page was actually read; found_official_info is false for that reason. Search-index snippets of the official lakebarrington.org water page reference a "Business Park Lead Notice, November 2019", annual Lake Barrington Industrial Park Water Quality Reports, and a president's letter titled "Is There Lead In Our Village Water?" (lakebarrington.org/news/6121) — contents unverified. Under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act, the village's small community system (IL0971080) was required to submit a complete service line material inventory to Illinois EPA by April 15, 2024; IEPA's page publishes no per-system inventory lookup and lists EPA.LeadandCopper@illinois.gov / (217) 785-0561 for inventory questions. Private-well homes (most of the village) are outside the Act's community-water-system inventory/replacement framework. No evidence of any village-funded replacement program was found.

lake-bluff.water_system: Village of Lake Bluff operates its own distribution system (39 miles of mains, maintained by Lake Bluff Public Works) but purchases all water from the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA), an intergovernmental cooperative; emergency interconnections with the City of Lake Forest.
lake-bluff.program_name: Village of Lake Bluff Lead Service Line Replacement Plan (draft plan required under ILSLRNA; not a branded program name)
lake-bluff.cost_coverage: Generally 50% of the replacement cost in Village-initiated projects (paid prior to construction) and 50% of the home-to-shut-off-box portion in water-main-project replacements (Village pays 100% between the shut-off box and the main); 0% in emergency-repair replacements; 100% if owner-initiated to upsize the service. Village's share is based on a 1-1/2 inch copper line, with any upsizing cost borne by the owner. Per the draft plan (April 15, 2024), the Village estimates the average replacement cost at $15,000 per service line ($1,740,000 total for the 116 lines identified at that time).
lake-bluff.homeowner_cost: Generally 50% of the replacement cost in Village-initiated projects (paid prior to construction) and 50% of the home-to-shut-off-box portion in water-main-project replacements; 0% in emergency-repair replacements; 100% if owner-initiated for a larger service. Village estimates average replacement cost at $15,000 per service line (total $1,740,000 for 116 lines).
lake-bluff.how_to_check_line: Review the "Service Line Inventory" document (as of April 2026) posted on the Village website; the Village also sent letters to properties identified with suspected/known lead lines. Residents with concerns who did not receive a letter can contact Village Engineer Jeff Hansen at 847-283-6884; the Village also suggests confirmation by a certified plumber.
lake-bluff.how_to_apply: No application form is published. Contact Village Engineer Jeff Hansen, 847-283-6884, or Village Hall, 40 E. Center Avenue, Lake Bluff, IL 60044, (847) 234-0774. Customer-initiated replacements require notifying the Village at least 45 days before work and securing a permit.
lake-bluff.notes: System has 1,992 service lines; 111 identified as lead or galvanized-requiring-replacement plus 5 unknown (116 requiring replacement); 8 lead lines replaced with copper since 2020. Under ILSLRNA/IEPA, mandatory replacement at 7% per year (minimum ~8 lines/year) begins in 2027 with all replacements complete by 2042. Replacements are triggered/coordinated with water main projects and emergency repairs; partial replacement is prohibited except access denial or emergencies (with filter provision). Draft plan submitted April 15, 2024 with annual updates; final plan due April 15, 2027. No loan or financing program is published. All identified lead lines are at residential buildings; none at schools or daycares. Water is corrosion-treated by CLCJAWA with 0.3 ppm orthophosphate; 2023 lead 90th percentile 5.4 ppb (action level 15 ppb).

lake-forest.water_system: Own system — the City of Lake Forest operates its own Water Plant (per the City's Lead in Service Lines FAQ, drinking water comes from the City of Lake Forest Water Plant); the City owns and operates approximately 168 miles of water mains
lake-forest.program_name: not named (a state-mandated multi-year lead service line replacement plan under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act, 415 ILCS 5/17.12)
lake-forest.cost_coverage: Full cost of replacing the service line falls on the homeowner: the City's page states "The entire portion of the water service line from the house to where it connects with the water main is owned by the homeowner" and "The maintenance and repair of that private water service line is the homeowner's responsibility," and the City FAQ answers "Who pays for replacement of service lines?" with "Service lines are not part of the public water system and are owned and maintained by the property owner." No city cost-share, subsidy, or free-replacement program is published on either official source; the only city concession is that permit fees for lead service line replacement are waived ("You will need a permit, but the City will waive any permit fees associated with replacing lead service lines"). Specific dollar figures are not published — the FAQ says cost depends on line length and location and that "A plumbing professional can best determine individual costs."
lake-forest.homeowner_cost: Full cost of replacing the (entirely privately owned) service line falls on the homeowner per official pages; specific dollar figures not published. The City waives permit fees for lead service line replacement.
lake-forest.how_to_check_line: Official lead service line identification map/dashboard linked from the City's Lead Service Line Replacement page (cityoflakeforest.com > Public Works); the City's inventory identifies roughly 400 properties that may have a privately owned lead service line, and in early 2024 the City mailed letters to inventoried homeowners to schedule verification inspections
lake-forest.how_to_apply: No application/enrollment process published. The City "strongly advises residents to hire a qualified contractor" and directs residents to Water & Sewer Supervisor Rich Volpe (volper@cityoflakeforest.com) for information and qualified-contractor guidance; the FAQ also lists J. Gulledge at the Water Plant (gulledgj@cityoflakeforest.com)
lake-forest.notes: Lake Forest's approach differs from many Chicago suburbs: the city has completed the state-required replacement plan (probable cost analysis, replacement schedule "within the required timeframe," inventory location map, public education) but publishes no city-funded replacement, cost-share, or loan program — replacement responsibility rests with homeowners. Per Illinois statute, when a lead service is repaired or upgraded the entire lead service must be replaced (no partial replacements). Lead is stated as not present in the City's treated water or its ~168 miles of mains. No coordination-with-water-main-project cost coverage, waitlist, or financing program is published.

lake-villa.how_to_apply: not published (no replacement program to apply to). For questions or line verification: Village Hall, 847-356-6100, Public Works / Water & Sewer department.
lake-villa.notes: Lake Villa is in the inventory stage only (as of the last available official page, Sept 2024): a community-wide Water Service Line Material Survey to identify lead lines and update the water meter inventory, driven by the federal/state mandate. No replacement schedule, waitlist, funding, loan program, or water-main-coordinated replacement policy is published. Caveat: the village recently migrated its website from lake-villa.org to villageoflakevilla.gov and the lead page has not (yet) been republished on the new site — the content above is the village's own page read via an archived snapshot; site search on the new domain returned no lead service line page. Residents should confirm current status at 847-356-6100. The page also notes lead usually comes from service lines/on-site plumbing, homes pre-1986 are most at risk, and the village performs IEPA-required distribution-system lead testing.

lake-zurich.water_system: The Village of Lake Zurich operates its own water system (IEPA system ID IL0970850), supplied by deep underground aquifers via six wells (five in regular use, one emergency backup) — not Lake Michigan and not a private utility.
lake-zurich.program_name: not named (official bid notice calls it the "2026-2027 Lead Service Line Replacement Project")
lake-zurich.cost_coverage: not published. The Village's official bid notice for the 2026-2027 Lead Service Line Replacement Project states the Village is contracting replacement at approximately 50-55 locations, "spanning both public and private sides, ranging from full service replacements (water main to meter) to partial replacements (b-box to meter/main)" — i.e., the Village-contracted work extends onto the private side to the meter — but no official page states whether property owners are billed any portion.
lake-zurich.how_to_check_line: The Village publishes its full address-level IEPA Water Service Line Material Inventory as a PDF (https://lakezurich.org/DocumentCenter/View/13636), listing each service address with PWS-side material, customer-side material, and classification (Lead/Non-Lead/Unknown). Current totals in the posted inventory: 6,884 total service lines, 33 lead, 6,840 non-lead, 9 unknown. No interactive map/portal is published; the Water Quality page directs questions to Utility Superintendent Steve Schmitt, 847-550-1773, steve.schmitt@lakezurich.org.
lake-zurich.how_to_apply: not published — no application form or sign-up process appears on official pages. The published contact for water/lead matters is Steve Schmitt, Utility Superintendent, 847-550-1773 / steve.schmitt@lakezurich.org (Public Works, 505 Telser Road).
lake-zurich.notes: Very small lead problem: only 33 lead + 9 unknown of 6,884 lines per the posted inventory, so the 2026-2027 project (approx. 50-55 locations: 25 already investigated plus 25-30 needing hydro-excavation/investigation) appears sized to address essentially all remaining lead lines. Bid timeline: documents available July 7, 2026 (QuestCDN, $22); mandatory pre-bid meeting July 22, 2026; bids due August 4, 2026; engineer is Atwell LLC. A prior Village capital project (Main Street/Whitney Road/Lake Zurich Drive water main, sewer and road improvements, approx. $13.2M, Copenhaver Construction) also included lead service line replacements, indicating LSL work is coordinated with water-main projects. The bid notice was located via the Daily Herald legal-notices marketplace but is a Village-issued notice; the Village's own bids page showed no open postings when checked. The Water Quality page also links "2025 Lead Tap Sampling Data" (https://lakezurich.org/DocumentCenter/View/13657/2025-Lead-Tap-Sampling-Data). No loan/grant program, waitlist, or homeowner cost-share terms are published on lakezurich.org.

libertyville.water_system: The Village of Libertyville operates its own distribution system (129 miles of water main, ~7,380 service connections, Facility ID IL0970900) and purchases treated Lake Michigan water from the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA), which adds orthophosphate as corrosion control.
libertyville.program_name: Two official items: (1) the Village "Lead Service Replacement Plan" (LSRP) — mandated Village-funded replacement program starting 2027; (2) the "Voluntary Lead Service Replacement Program," formalized as Administrative Policy No. 16-01 ("Residential Lead Service Replacement Incentive Program"), for owners who don't want to wait.
libertyville.cost_coverage: Village-run LSRP (2027-2036): "It is currently proposed that the Village will assume the entire cost of replacing the lead service lines" — the Hold Harmless Agreement describes "the Village's performance of the Work solely at the Village's cost and expense," replacing the line "in its entirety, including any portion of the service line running on private property," per the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act (415 ILCS 5/17.12); the Village will handle permitting and waive all permit fees (a meter upgrade fee might still be required case-by-case). Note this is the currently proposed/anticipated funding approach — the plan states annual costs would be funded by an IEPA low-interest loan and an adjustment of water rates across the entire customer base, with payment plans considered for customers having financial difficulty. Voluntary program (available now, Admin Policy 16-01): "Reimbursement is for 50% of construction cost, up to $2,500 (partial replacement to valve) or $6,000 (full replacement to public main)," with the reimbursement based on the lowest responsible of 3 contractor quotes and conditioned on compliance with all permit requirements and Village restoration standards; no permit fees are charged, though a meter upgrade fee and refundable deposit may apply, and the homeowner hires the contractor and pays the balance. Under both paths, LSRP work stops at the water meter and excludes sewer lines and repair of finished areas (drywall, plaster, cabinets, carpet, flooring, etc.), which remain the homeowner's sole responsibility.
libertyville.homeowner_cost: Under the Village LSRP (starting 2027): currently proposed to be $0 — the Village currently proposes to assume the entire cost, to be funded via an IEPA low-interest loan and water-rate adjustments across the customer base (payment plans considered for customers with financial difficulty); this funding approach is a proposal and could change. Under the Voluntary program: the homeowner hires the contractor and pays the balance after the Village reimburses 50% of construction cost, capped at $2,500 (partial, to the B-box valve) or $6,000 (full, to the public main), based on the lowest responsible of 3 contractor quotes and conditioned on compliance with all permit requirements and Village restoration standards; a meter upgrade fee and refundable deposit may apply. LSRP work stops at the water meter and excludes sewer lines and repair of finished areas (drywall, flooring, etc.), which remain the homeowner's responsibility.
libertyville.how_to_check_line: Official public "Water Service Material Inventory" interactive ArcGIS dashboard: https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/29b7db18bb2d4ad48637fc7f50a4e912. Residents can also request an in-home verification appointment from Village staff by calling the Utilities Division at (847) 362-3434.
libertyville.how_to_apply: Village LSRP: no action needed — "No action is needed at this time to be included in this program"; the Village sends pre-construction notification letters and a Hold Harmless Agreement when an address is scheduled. Voluntary program: first step is an inspection by Village staff to confirm a lead service inside the home — call the Utilities Division, (847) 362-3434, M-F 7am-3:30pm; then obtain 3 contractor quotes and secure Building Division ((847) 918-2020) and Engineering Division ((847) 918-2100) permits. Program contact: Harrison Meyer, P.E., Senior Project Engineer, hmeyer@libertyville.com, (847) 367-7054.
libertyville.notes: Inventory as of the 4/13/2026 plan revision: 331 confirmed lead and 537 unknown of 7,380 connections; plan assumes 868 services need replacement (~87-89/year over 10 years, est. $1.5M/year). Phased schedule: Phase I (2027) ~90 known partial replacements; Phase II (2028-2033) village streets street-by-street, ~630 services, coordinated with the Annual Water Main Replacement program ($4-5M/yr combined); Phase III (2034-2035) state/county routes ~100; Phase IV (2036) downtown/Milwaukee Ave ~70 with new water main. Refusing LSLR work requires signing a formal waiver. Plan originally issued April 7, 2025, last revised April 13, 2026. The full-coverage statement is "currently proposed" and 2027 program details could change; the voluntary 50% cost-share is the option in effect today.

lincolnshire.water_system: Village of Lincolnshire operates its own distribution system and purchases Lake Michigan water from the City of Highland Park (connection initiated in 1982); distribution mains are predominantly ductile iron
lincolnshire.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's official Lead and Copper Information page states "To date, the utility department has not identified any lead service lines in the Village water system," and publishes no replacement program or cost-coverage policy
lincolnshire.how_to_check_line: not published — no public service-line inventory map or lookup portal found on lincolnshireil.gov; page directs lead/copper questions to Maxwell Geib, Utilities Superintendent, 847-913-2383
lincolnshire.how_to_apply: not published (no program exists per official pages); contact for lead/copper drinking water questions: Maxwell Geib, Utilities Superintendent, Public Works Department, 847-913-2383
lincolnshire.notes: Official Village position: no lead service lines have been identified in the water system to date, and the Village is in full compliance with all IEPA drinking-water regulations. The Village samples water from selected homes for lead and copper every three years. Residents with concerns may request testing via certified labs, use approved filters, and flush taps after water sits stagnant. Highland Park (the wholesale supplier) handles source-water testing. No LSLR program, timeline, waitlist, rebate, loan, or main-project-coordinated replacement is published — consistent with a system reporting zero identified lead lines under the Illinois LSLR and Notification Act.

lincolnwood.water_system: Village of Lincolnwood operates its own municipal water system (IEPA ID IL0311650); source water is Lake Michigan (purchased supply — the Village's official water quality report references City of Evanston's treatment plant data, including Evanston's PFAS results page)
lincolnwood.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement Rebate Program (plus a Village-led Lead Service Line Replacement Plan/Project)
lincolnwood.cost_coverage: Two tracks per official pages: (1) Village-led project — Lincolnwood's Lead Service Line Replacement Project is "fully funded through the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (SRF) as part of the Public Water Supply Loan Program," backed by a $6.2 million IEPA Public Water Supply Loan Program loan. The Village describes ownership as split — "Village-owned portion: From the water main to the Buffalo Box (B-Box)" and "Property owner-owned portion: From the B-Box or exterior water meter into the home or building" — but the official pages do NOT state that owners must pay for the private portion under this project; the Village says "no action is required" and warns that letters requesting funding for lead service lines may be a scam. (2) Rebate track — for owner-initiated replacements the Village provides "a cost-match of 50% of the total project up to a maximum of $5,000," covering partial (water meter/buffalo box to interior connection) or full (water main to interior connection) replacements; interior restoration costs are NOT covered; funds are limited and awarded first-come, first-served. Homeowner cost: under the rebate program the homeowner pays the remainder after the 50% cost-match (max $5,000) plus all interior restoration costs; for the SRF-funded Village-led project the pages publish no homeowner out-of-pocket cost, and residents are advised that no action or payment is required of them.
lincolnwood.homeowner_cost: Under the rebate program the homeowner pays roughly 50% of the replacement cost (Village cost-match is 50% up to $5,000) plus all interior restoration costs. For the SRF-funded Village-led project the official pages publish no homeowner out-of-pocket cost — the Village states the project is "fully funded through the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (SRF)," that "no action is required" of residents, and warns that letters requesting funding for lead service lines may be a scam.
lincolnwood.how_to_check_line: Official Lead Service Line Inventory page (lincolnwoodil.org/512) links an interactive ArcGIS dashboard/mapping tool to look up a property's service line material, plus a downloadable inventory PDF (IL0311650 Village of Lincolnwood Inventory, 4-15-2025) and a Water Service Material Survey; also lincolnwoodil.org/308/Water-Service-Line-Information and wsrp.cbbel.com/village-of-lincolnwood. In July 2025 the Village mailed letters to all addresses with identified lead lines.
lincolnwood.how_to_apply: Rebate: complete the application (PDF) on the Village website's lead service line replacement section; questions to the Public Works Department at 847-675-0888 (Mon-Fri 8:00AM-4:00PM). Village-led project: no application — the Village states "no action is required" for residents who received notification letters; general Public Works contact 847-673-1540, 6900 N Lincoln Avenue.
lincolnwood.notes: Per the official replacement plan page: ~1,114 lead service lines remained as of 2024; replacements were 23 lines in 2023, 37 in 2024, ~173 estimated in 2025, ~133 estimated in 2026; the Village cites a state-mandated completion deadline (511 page says 2037 for full completion, while search summaries of other Village pages cite the LSLRNA 2042 statewide deadline). Initial replacement plan submitted to IEPA April 15, 2024. Village received a $6.2M IEPA Public Water Supply Loan Program loan; the Village-led project is fully SRF-funded. Rebate funds are limited, first-come first-served. Program driven by the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act (415 ILCS 5/17.12).

lindenhurst.water_system: Village of Lindenhurst operates its own distribution system (IEPA system 0971000); since 2017 it purchases Lake Michigan water, pre-treated, from the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA), with backup emergency wells. Village Public Works: (847) 356-8252.
lindenhurst.cost_coverage: not published (homeowner owns and is responsible for the private portion from the curb stop/b-box into the home; no dollar figures, subsidy, or village-paid replacement program is published). Note: per Illinois statute cited on the page, when a lead service is repaired or upgraded the entire lead service line must be replaced, so a repair on either portion can trigger full replacement; the statutory replacement plan (draft 2024, final by 2027) must include a probable cost analysis and low-income financing options, but those are not yet published.
lindenhurst.homeowner_cost: not published (homeowner owns and is responsible for the private portion from curb stop into the home; no dollar figures or subsidy published)
lindenhurst.how_to_check_line: Village asks residents to self-identify exposed pipe at the basement entry using scratch test (lead = shiny silver, copper = penny color, galvanized = dull gray), magnet test (sticks only to galvanized), and tapping test (lead = dull sound), then submit the Village's online Unknown Water Service Line Survey; the official IEPA service line inventory (April 2025/2026 update PDFs) is posted on the Village site. No interactive address-lookup map is published.
lindenhurst.how_to_apply: No application process exists (no replacement program yet). Residents with unknown lines complete the Unknown Water Service Line Survey or call Public Works at (847) 356-8252; the Village began mailing letters to owners of unknown lines in May 2024.
lindenhurst.notes: Key facts from the official inventory page: ~5,200 total service lines inventoried (with vendor 120 Water); ~1,100 remain "unknown" material; "To date, Lindenhurst Public Works has not identified any lead service lines" — materials found are copper, galvanized iron, and plastic. Because no lead lines have been confirmed, there is no active replacement program; the Village is in the identification phase. Per the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act (415 ILCS 5/17.12) the Village submitted/must submit a draft replacement plan in 2024 and a final plan by 2027, which must include a replacement schedule, map, cost analysis, and low-income financing options. Water source is Lake Michigan via CLCJAWA since 2017. Posted documents include the 2026 IEPA Official Service Line Inventory and 2025 Lead and Copper sampling results.

long-grove.water_system: Village of Long Grove operates its own small municipal water system (PWS ID IL0970340, groundwater from two deep wells) serving ONLY the historic downtown and surrounding area — built with the Sunset Grove Development in the late 2000s and expanded to the downtown 2016-2019; operated under contract by Gewalt Hamilton Associates, Inc. The rest of the village is outside this system (official pages note many residences are on private septic and the municipal system serves only downtown; properties elsewhere are not on village water).
long-grove.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's water system pages and Consumer Confidence Report contain no lead service line replacement program or cost-coverage policy. The only cost policy published is unrelated: buildings within 80 ft of the downtown watermain must connect, with an optional Special Service Area for financing the connection (minimum quarterly water rate $100).
long-grove.how_to_check_line: not published — no service line material inventory map or portal on longgroveil.gov. The CCR directs water quality questions to the Village (847-634-9440) or its consultant Gewalt Hamilton Associates (847-478-9700); current water quality contact is Mike Grinnell, mgrinnell@gha-engineers.com, 847-309-5438. Illinois EPA's lead service line page lists EPA.LeadandCopper@illinois.gov / 217-785-0561 for inventory questions.
long-grove.how_to_apply: not published — no program exists per official sources; contact Village Hall, 3110 Old McHenry Road, 847-634-9440, or water system contact Mike Grinnell (Gewalt Hamilton), 847-309-5438.
long-grove.notes: The municipal water system dates entirely from the late 2000s-2019 (per the Village's Roads & Utilities page), i.e., built long after lead service lines were banned — but the Village publishes no lead service line inventory or replacement content, so no material determination is stated officially. CCR 2021: lead 90th percentile 3.3 ppb, 0 sites over the 15 ppb action level; lead language is the generic EPA household-plumbing advisory only. The live longgroveil.gov site is behind a Cloudflare challenge; official pages were read via Wayback Machine archives (water system page captured 2025-03-04, Roads & Utilities 2025-12-31). LSLRNA inventory filings for IL0970340 would be with Illinois EPA; IEPA's public lead service line page has no resident-facing lookup displayed. Small non-village community supplies also exist within Long Grove (e.g., HOA well systems), which would file their own inventories.

long-lake.water_system: Long Lake is an unincorporated community/CDP (Grant, Avon, and Lake Villa Townships, Lake County) with no municipal government. Illinois EPA's Drinking Water Watch shows NO community water system named "Long Lake" (search returned 0 records), so the area has no water system of its own. Lake County Public Works operates county drinking-water systems and a service line map for its customers, but its announcement notes that residents "receiving water from local villages or private wells" are not LCPW customers; LCPW does not list Long Lake as a served area. Adjacent official systems are the Village of Fox Lake (2 mi west) and Round Lake Beach (borders east/south). Which supplier (if any, vs. private wells) serves a given Long Lake address was not published on any official page reviewed.
long-lake.cost_coverage: not published — no official lead service line replacement program exists for Long Lake itself (no municipality, no water system). The nearest official page, Village of Fox Lake's "Lead Service Line Information," publishes only a lead pipe study/inventory map ("This map is only to be considered a general guide") and states the Village "is currently in compliance with all state and federal regulations regarding lead"; it describes no replacement program and no cost-sharing.
long-lake.how_to_check_line: No Long Lake-specific inventory exists. If served by Village of Fox Lake: view its Lead Service Line Inventory map at foxlake.org/305/Lead-Service-Line-Information or call the Sewer and Water Division at (847) 587-3506. If a Lake County Public Works customer: use the LCPW interactive water service line map or call 847-377-7500. Private well owners are outside the Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act's community-water-supply inventory requirement.
long-lake.how_to_apply: not published — no program to apply to. Contacts: Village of Fox Lake Sewer and Water Division (847) 587-3506; Lake County Public Works (847) 377-7500.
long-lake.notes: Long Lake is a census-designated place, not a village, so there is no "village pays" program comparable to incorporated Chicago suburbs. The Long Lake Improvement and Sanitation Association (llisa.org) is a lake/watershed association (dam, lake cleanup, fish stocking) — it is not a drinking-water utility and publishes nothing about service lines. The Lake County Public Works service line map bulletin covers only LCPW's own drinking-water systems and discusses inventory/self-identification, not replacement or cost. Whether a specific Long Lake address is on a private well, Fox Lake water, or Round Lake Beach water must be confirmed with those providers; the applicable inventory/replacement obligations under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act follow that supplier. The lakecountyil.gov Water Distribution Systems page is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be read directly.

melrose-park.water_system: Village of Melrose Park operates its own community water system (IL EPA ID 0311860, "Melrose Park Water Department"). Source is Lake Michigan water purchased from the City of Chicago: per the Village's 2024 CCR, "The City of Chicago Water Department provides the water treatment necessary to safeguard the water delivered to Melrose Park," delivered via Chicago's Springfield Pumping Station to the Village's connection at Harlem and Wabansia, then through Village reservoirs/pumping stations into local distribution. Melrose Park in turn wholesales water to neighboring systems (Bellwood, Maywood, Stone Park, Northlake, Hillside-Berkeley Water Commission, Leyden Township — per IL EPA grant announcement, not restated on the Village site).
melrose-park.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's official pages (Public Works page and 2024 Consumer Confidence Report) do not describe any lead service line replacement program or say who pays for replacements. A state legislator announcement notes Melrose Park received a $50,000 Illinois EPA grant, but that grant is for inventorying/mapping service lines, not replacement, and the Village site itself does not mention it.
melrose-park.how_to_check_line: The Village posts a "Lead Service Line Inventory Map (2026)" (https://www.melrosepark.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Lead_Service-Line-Inventory-Map-2026.pdf) and a "Lead Service Line Inventory Spreadsheet (2026)" (https://www.melrosepark.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Lead-Service-Line-Inventory-Spreadsheet-2026.pdf) on its Public Works page — residents look up their address in these PDF documents. No interactive portal is published.
melrose-park.how_to_apply: not published — no application process is listed. General contact: Public Works Department, 1000 N. 25th Avenue, Melrose Park, IL 60160, (708) 343-5128 (Mon-Fri 9am-5pm); Water Superintendent Mike Carpanzano, (708) 531-5360.
melrose-park.notes: Melrose Park has complied with the Illinois LSLR&N Act's inventory requirement (2026 inventory map + spreadsheet published May 2026) but publishes no replacement plan, no cost-sharing policy, no timeline, and no water-main-coordination details on melrosepark.org. The 2024 CCR (for 2023) reports lead 90th percentile of 3 ppb across 30 sampled homes, 0 sites over the 15 ppb action level, no violations. The Public Works page also links a Lead-Copper Report (2023). Residents wanting replacement details must call Public Works at (708) 343-5128. Note: a 2021 melrosepark.org "ATTENTION RESIDENTS - CALL TO REQUEST REPLACEMENT" PDF that surfaces in searches is about garbage/recycling cans, not water lines.

morton-grove.water_system: Village of Morton Grove operates its own water division; Lake Michigan water is purchased via the Morton Grove-Niles Water Commission, which obtains it from the City of Evanston's treatment plant (555 Lincoln St, Evanston).
morton-grove.program_name: not named (referred to only as lead service line replacement under the Village's Water Quality Information / Lead & Copper Rule Revision inventory effort)
morton-grove.cost_coverage: Homeowner pays the cost of hiring a licensed plumber to replace the private portion of the service line "from the meter to the property's B-box" (the sources require homeowners to "contract individually with a licensed plumber" and list no financial assistance, so full homeowner payment is implied rather than stated outright). For homeowners who received a lead notification and choose to replace, the Village waives the permit fee and provides "complete restoration of the public right-of-way portion of your replacement project," and homeowners are told to coordinate with the Public Works Water Department so the Village-owned portion (water main to B-box) is replaced at the same time. Replacement is voluntary; no dollar figures, grants, reimbursements, income limits, or caps are published.
morton-grove.homeowner_cost: Homeowner pays the full cost of hiring a licensed plumber for the private portion (B-box/meter to house); the Village waives the permit fee and restores the public right-of-way. No dollar figures, grants, or reimbursement amounts are published.
morton-grove.how_to_check_line: Official self-identification: locate the pipe entering the basement/utility room, scratch-test it per the Village's visual guide (mortongroveil.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/water-service-line.pdf), then report via the Water Service Line Material Survey (ArcGIS Survey123 portal).
