The compiled inventory summary is viewable on an ArcGIS dashboard linked from the Water Quality Information page. Public Works also delivered door tags/letters to homes 2022-2024 to build the inventory.
morton-grove.how_to_apply: Contact Morton Grove Public Works (Water Department) to coordinate replacement of the Village-owned portion and the permit-fee waiver; no dedicated application form is published — homeowner arranges their own licensed plumber for the private side.
morton-grove.notes: No published timeline, waitlist, loan/grant program, or full-cost village replacement — this is a homeowner-initiated model with village-side coordination, unlike suburbs that replace private portions during water-main projects. Inventory was built 2022-2024 via door tags and a resident Survey123 form per the Lead & Copper Rule Revision. Age guidance published: pre-1930 homes likely lead; 1930-1960 lead or copper; post-1960 likely copper. A 2024 "Emergency Lead Line Replacement Program" bid solicitation exists (illinoisbids.com listing), suggesting village contracting for emergency replacements, but details are not on official pages so not relied upon.

mount-prospect.water_system: The Village of Mount Prospect operates its own community water system for most of the village; official pages state that some residents are in the Illinois American Water service area and must contact Illinois American (amwater.com/ilaw) about lead service lines — Illinois American customers and private-well owners are not eligible for the Village's program.
mount-prospect.program_name: Lead and Galvanized Steel Water Service Replacement Cost Sharing Program
mount-prospect.cost_coverage: Official page: "The Village will reimburse 100% of the cost to replace the service line from the water main to the water shutoff valve, known as the B-box. And 2/3 of the cost to replace the shutoff valve to the water meter, but not more than $10,000 of the actual expenses incurred. Low-income homeowners may be eligible for a 0% interest deferred loan." Program covers replacing lead or galvanized steel service with copper from the public water main to the water meter inside the property; homeowners, multi-family, and commercial buildings are eligible. Eligibility is limited to Village of Mount Prospect water customers — Illinois American Water Company customers and residents with privately owned wells are not eligible. Homeowner pays 1/3 of the B-box-to-water-meter (private) portion, any amount above the $10,000 reimbursement cap, plus Village permit fees and bonds ("All Applicable permit fees and bonds will apply"). Only work performed with a valid Village of Mount Prospect permit is considered, and the program is not retroactive — work performed in the past is not eligible; the Village advises contacting Public Works (847-870-5640) before commencing any work.
mount-prospect.homeowner_cost: Homeowner pays 1/3 of the B-box-to-water-meter (private) portion, any amount above the $10,000 reimbursement cap, plus Village permit fees and bonds ("All applicable permit fees and bonds will apply"). Work must be done under a valid Village of Mount Prospect permit; the program is not retroactive — past work is not eligible.
mount-prospect.how_to_check_line: The Village's Lead Service Inspection Program page offers an interactive map of all lead service line locations within the Village's water service area, and Public Works conducts free in-home plumbing inspections (about 5 minutes) to determine service line material — schedule by calling 847-870-5640. Illinois American Water area residents must contact Illinois American instead.
mount-prospect.how_to_apply: Contact Public Works BEFORE commencing any work: 847-870-5640 or publicworksdept@mountprospect.org. Technical/installation questions: Village Plumbing Inspector 847-870-5675. Work requires a permit from the Building and Inspection Services Department. Program documents (program description, SOP, IDPH waiver form) are linked on the program page.
mount-prospect.notes: Inventory driven by the Illinois EPA mandate (415 ILCS 5) for a comprehensive service line inventory; residents who receive a letter are asked to schedule the free inspection. The Village page explicitly warns about a misleading GreenTech Plumbing solicitation letter and states the Village cost-share program "does not fund 100% of the replacement costs." Search results attribute to the Village's Water Main Improvements page a statement that during water main improvement projects the Village replaces the entire lead service line (main to meter) at no cost with a signed opt-out waiver, but that live page returns 403 and its archived copies predate the statement, so it could not be verified quote-level from an official page actually read. mountprospect.org blocks automated fetches (Akamai 403); content above was read from Wayback Machine snapshots of the official pages dated 2026-03-16 (cost-share) and 2026-05-13 (inspection program).

mundelein.water_system: Village of Mundelein operates its own water system: four Lake Michigan water receiving and distribution stations, plus two well water stations as standby sources. Village states its water mains are lead-free.
mundelein.program_name: not named (only a "Lead Service Line Identification Initiative" / Water Service Line Material survey is published)
mundelein.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's lead service line page states "the water service lines are owned by individual property owners, from the water main in the street to the water meter in the home," and publishes no cost-sharing or village-funded replacement program
mundelein.how_to_check_line: Official Lead Service Line Survey page offers: (1) Mundelein Service Line Inventory Map dashboard (arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/0cf1ef2c1edd4ef3adc363a62e57f739), (2) a "Water Service Line Material" self-report survey (survey123.arcgis.com/share/075d6776ddab46658252ba21437c6d4c), (3) instructions to scratch/magnet-test the pipe at the water meter
mundelein.how_to_apply: No application process published; contact Village of Mundelein Water Division at 847-949-3273
mundelein.notes: Mundelein's official pages cover only the federally/state-mandated identification phase: a resident survey and a public ArcGIS service line inventory map. No replacement program, cost coverage, timeline, waitlist, or water-main-project coordination is published. Since the village says service lines are owned by property owners main-to-meter, replacement responsibility currently appears to rest with homeowners absent a future program. Homes built before 1986 are flagged as most likely to have lead lines.

niles.water_system: Village of Niles operates its own distribution system (103 miles of mains, its own reservoirs/tanks) but purchases Lake Michigan drinking water from the City of Evanston through the Morton Grove-Niles Water Commission.
niles.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Pilot Program
niles.cost_coverage: $0 for the 315-home pilot (homes were pre-selected by Illinois EPA criteria — residents could not opt in, and the Right-of-Entry deadline was March 1, 2025) and $0 for full replacements when a lead line is disturbed during a leak repair. The Village also runs "a few annual replacement projects" each year (participation via Public Works, (847) 588-7900; cost not published). Outside these programs, an older Village page says there is no replacement program and directs homeowners to contract individually with licensed plumbers — cost not published.
niles.homeowner_cost: $0 for the 315-home pilot and for full replacements when a lead line is disturbed during a leak repair; homeowners outside these programs are not covered (an older Village page directs them to contract licensed plumbers independently — cost not published).
niles.how_to_check_line: Official interactive Lead Service Inventory map (ArcGIS app linked from vniles.com/1554/Lead-Line-Replacement) — enter house number to see material type; discrepancies: call the Village at (847) 600-LEAD. Village also suggests inspecting accessible plumbing yourself or hiring a plumber.
niles.how_to_apply: Pilot is Village-selected (315 homes chosen per Illinois EPA criteria); selected residents receive a mailing and must submit a Right-of-Entry form at www.vniles.com/leadsafety or by calling 847-600-LEAD (pilot deadline was March 1, 2025). For future projects, contact Public Works at (847) 588-7900; general Village contact 847-588-8000 / ContactNiles@vniles.com.
niles.notes: Village has been proactively replacing lead lines since 2022. Pilot (315 homes, $4M zero-interest IEPA SRF loan) is described as "the first phase of our 12-year plan" toward the federal 2037 replacement mandate. Each line replacement takes about eight hours with 24-hour notice before service disruption. Note: an older Village page (vniles.com/1066) still states "The Village currently does not have a program to replace water services" — superseded by the newer Lead Line Replacement page (vniles.com/1554). Total lead line count and cost figures ($69.7M, 4,100-4,700 lines) appeared only in search snippets/news, not verified on official pages, so treat as unconfirmed. Village states lead is not found in its source water or distribution system.

norridge.water_system: Village of Norridge operates its own Water Department (approx. 5,100 customers, ~1.5 million gallons/day); per the Village's annual Water Quality Report page, "The Village of Norridge purchases all of its drinking water from the City of Chicago."
norridge.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's Lead Service Lines page only describes the state mandate: the LSLRNA (Public Act 102-0613) requires "owners and operators of community water supplies to develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive water service line material inventory and replacement plan." No village-specific replacement program, cost-sharing, or reimbursement terms are published.
norridge.how_to_check_line: The Village publishes a downloadable "Inventory of Water Service Lines" document (linked from the Lead Service Lines page) listing each service address with PWS-side and customer-side line material and classification; it reports 4,844 total service lines: 50 lead, 4,586 non-lead, 208 unknown. The page also links "2023 Lead / Copper Sample Sites Results" and gettheleadoutil.com.
norridge.how_to_apply: not published — no application/program form exists on the official site; Water Department contact is 708-453-0319, 4000 N Olcott Ave, Norridge, IL 60706 (Mon–Fri 9 AM–5 PM, Sat 9 AM–noon)
norridge.notes: Official Lead Service Lines page content is limited to explaining the Illinois LSLRNA (effective Jan 1, 2022) plus the inventory and sampling-results downloads — no published replacement schedule, cost coverage, waitlist, or water-main-project coordination. The inventory shows only 50 confirmed lead lines out of 4,844 (about 1%), with 208 unknown. The village website (villageofnorridge.com) blocks automated fetches (Akamai 403); content was verified via Feb/May 2026 Wayback Machine captures of the official pages. A 2022 resident lead service line self-report survey was referenced in a third-party press-release listing but could not be verified on the official site, so it is not reported as current.

north-barrington.water_system: The Village of North Barrington does not operate a municipal water system. Official village pages reference only private wells and individual septic systems (the Health Department handles septic permits and "Septic & Well" information; the village lists no water utility or public works water department). The IEPA Drinking Water Watch portal shows one active community groundwater system associated with the village: "Wynstone Water Company" (IEPA system ID IL0970080, Lake County, groundwater), a private utility serving the Wynstone subdivision.
north-barrington.cost_coverage: not published — no lead service line program or cost information appears anywhere on the Village of North Barrington's official website
north-barrington.how_to_check_line: not published — no service line inventory map or portal exists on the village site. Most homes are on private wells, which have no utility-owned service line; residents on the private Wynstone Water Company system would need to contact that utility for its IEPA-required inventory.
north-barrington.how_to_apply: not published — no program exists. General village contact: (847) 381-6000; Health Officer Natalie Karney (nkarney@northbarrington.org) handles well/septic matters.
north-barrington.notes: North Barrington is a low-density village where homes overwhelmingly use private wells and septic systems, so the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act's inventory/replacement obligations largely do not apply at the village level (the Act applies to community water supplies). The one community water supply identified via the official IEPA Drinking Water Watch portal is the private Wynstone Water Company (ID IL0970080); its lead service line inventory/plan, if any, is not published on any village page reviewed. Note: the nearby Village of Barrington (a separate municipality, barrington-il.gov) has its own IEPA-grant-funded no-cost replacement program and inventory map — it does not serve North Barrington and should not be conflated with it. The village site mentions BACOG private well water testing events as the well-water quality resource for residents.

northbrook.water_system: Village of Northbrook operates its own water system: "the Village pumps water directly from Lake Michigan and provides all treatment necessary to make it safe to use and drink" — village-owned Water Plant operating around the clock.
northbrook.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement Cost Share Program
northbrook.cost_coverage: Homeowner pays the private-side portion (b-box/shut-off valve to house foundation) minus a Village reimbursement of up to 50% of the low bid or $5,000, whichever is less; the public-side portion (water main to b-box/shut-off valve) is fully reimbursed by the Village. On water main replacement projects, the Village reimburses up to 50% (max $5,000) of the cost of replacing the lead line between the shut-off valve and the water meter. Permit fees are waived, but a permit and passing final inspection are required for reimbursement, work must be completed within 90 calendar days of low-bid approval, and cost-share participation is first-come, first-served subject to funds available in the Village Annual Budget.
northbrook.homeowner_cost: Homeowner pays the private-side portion (b-box/shut-off valve to house foundation) minus the Village reimbursement of up to 50% of the low bid or $5,000, whichever is less; the public-side portion (main to b-box) is fully reimbursed by the Village. Permit fees are waived, but reimbursement requires obtaining a permit and passing final inspection, all projects must be completed within 90 calendar days of approval of the lowest bid, and participation is first-come, first-served subject to funds available in the Village Annual Budget.
northbrook.how_to_check_line: Official interactive service line inventory map (ArcGIS): https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/1dbdb00ae7474d25a9c14342064f9462, linked from the Village's Lead Service Line Inventory page (published per 415 ILCS 5/17.12). Where owners don't respond to surveys, the Village may excavate at the buffalo-box to determine the material.
northbrook.how_to_apply: Submit the Lead Water Service Application Packet (https://www.northbrook.il.us/DocumentCenter/View/6509/Lead-Water-Service-Application-Packet) before work begins; apply prior to the work starting. Questions: Public Works Department, 847-272-4711. A permit from Development and Planning Services is required (fees waived); work must be inspected by the Village Plumbing Inspector.
northbrook.notes: Participation is first-come, first-served, subject to funds allocated in the Village Annual Budget. Projects must be completed within 90 calendar days from approval of the lowest bid. The Village incorporates lead service line replacement into water main replacement project bids so homeowners can piggyback on village contracts. Inventory as of April 15, 2025: 12,554 total service lines, 282 lead, 12,272 non-lead; no lead water mains in the distribution system (lead services mostly in homes built before the mid-1950s). State-mandated full replacement plan due April 15, 2027 (specifics still being discussed); Illinois Act requires all lead service lines replaced by 2042 with a minimum 7% annual replacement rate from April 2027; initial plan submitted April 15, 2024 with annual updates each April.

northfield.water_system: The Village of Northfield operates its own community water supply/distribution system but purchases its water from the Village of Winnetka, whose source is Lake Michigan surface water (per the Village's 2024 Annual Drinking Water Quality Report). The Village's own program applies to homes connected to a Village of Northfield maintained water main.
northfield.program_name: Lead Service Line (LSL) Replacement Program (the cost-share component is called the Lead Service Line Replacement Reimbursement Program)
northfield.cost_coverage: Homeowner pays the full replacement cost up front (proof of payment required) and is reimbursed 50% of eligible costs based on the lowest of three licensed-plumber estimates, capped at $10,000 — i.e., the homeowner bears at least 50% plus anything over the cap and all ineligible costs (architectural/engineering/professional fees, interior repairs, driveways/private sidewalks, decorative plantings/hardscape, private electrical, temporary water facilities, deposits, any costs not in the original quote or exceeding the $10,000 max; the Village street/parkway opening bond is not waived, though Village permit fees are). Funding is limited — the Village budgets roughly 10 replacements per year, first-come, first-served, and only homes connected to a Village-maintained main and listed on the Village's Lead Service Line Inventory qualify; work must be completed within 90 days of permit issuance. In Village water-main projects/repairs, the Village replaces main-to-b-box and the homeowner is required to replace b-box-to-meter; if emergency repairs to a private lead line are needed, the homeowner must replace the entire line from main to meter within a Village-determined timeframe — homeowners in either situation get priority in the reimbursement program for that fiscal year, so they can still claim the 50%/$10,000 reimbursement.
northfield.homeowner_cost: Homeowner pays the full replacement cost up front and is reimbursed 50% of eligible costs (based on the lowest of three estimates), capped at $10,000 — i.e., the homeowner bears at least 50% plus anything over the cap and all ineligible costs (professional fees, interior repairs, driveways/private sidewalks, plantings/hardscape, temporary water facilities, deposits, costs exceeding the $10,000 max; the street/parkway opening bond is not waived). In Village water-main projects, the Village replaces main-to-b-box and the homeowner must pay to replace b-box-to-meter; if emergency repairs to a private lead line are needed, the homeowner must replace the entire line from main to meter within a Village-determined timeframe.
northfield.how_to_check_line: Consult the Village's Lead Service Line Inventory Map / "Properties with Lead Service" list (https://www.northfieldil.org/DocumentCenter/View/2804/, dated 12-30-24), linked from the LSL Replacement Program page; lead tap sampling data and inventory copies are available from Bill Wipperfurth, Public Works Department, (847) 441-3810.
northfield.how_to_apply: Submit the Lead Service Line Replacement Program Application (in the program document at https://www.northfieldil.org/DocumentCenter/View/2595/) with: three detailed written estimates from licensed plumbing contractors, a Contractor Checklist from the chosen contractor, completed plumbing permit applications, and three copies of construction plans. Work must be completed within 90 days of permit issuance and pass Village inspections; then submit a Reimbursement Request form with proof of payment. Questions: Building Department, (847) 784-3551.
northfield.notes: Program effective May 1, 2024; voluntary. Goal is replacing 12.5% of existing lead service lines per year over 8 years (~10 replacements/year budgeted) — the LSL Replacement Program page states all lead water services must be replaced by 2042. Funds are first-come, first-served with an annually set budget. Eligibility requires connection to a Village-maintained water main and listing on the Village's LSL Inventory; full main-to-home replacement (plus a new Village-specified AMI meter if needed) is required, and downstream galvanized lines connected to lead must also be fully replaced. Retroactive reimbursement is available for replacements done between January 1, 2023 and the program's effective date. Homeowners forced to replace due to Village main projects/repairs or emergency repairs get priority for that fiscal year. Homeowners who sign a risk-acceptance waiver instead of replacing are ineligible for reimbursement after the 8-year program window. No loan program is published. 2023 90th-percentile lead result was 3.4 ppb (no action-level exceedance at that time); a Village Drinking Water Notification (Jan 2026, per the Village site) reported that sampling of 35 lead-service-line homes found more than 10% exceeded 15 ppb.

northlake.water_system: Northlake operates its own municipal water system (Public Works Department). Per the city's Dec 2024-Jan 2025 newsletter, a new interconnection with the Village of Franklin Park's water system ensures "the City has two sources of water through Melrose Park and Franklin Park" (Lake Michigan water); a city news article titled "Chicago Unilaterally Raises Water Rates" indicates Chicago is the upstream supplier.
northlake.program_name: Not formally named; the city's public-facing site is the "City of Northlake Lead Safe Community" hub (lead-norlkpw.hub.arcgis.com), described as "an ArcGIS Hub site used to communicate our lead service line replacement program"
northlake.cost_coverage: City pays for the full replacement including the privately owned portion. City lead-service-line page (now offline; wording preserved in search-index text of northlakecity.com/lead-water-service-line): "The law provides that the City may charge the property owner for the cost of replacement, however, the City of Northlake's position is that even though the water service line belongs to the property owner, the City will replace and pay for the new copper line." Mayor in the city's 2026 infrastructure article (live, verified): "We will continue to replace lead water services this year at no cost to the resident. Our goal is 200 replacements for 2026." City newsletters confirm the City itself funded prior rounds (81 replacements in 2024 at approximately $600,000). No income limits, caps, or water-main-project-only conditions appear in any source.
northlake.homeowner_cost: $0 — "at no cost to the resident" per the city's 2026 infrastructure news article; the city replaces and pays for the new copper line even though the service line belongs to the property owner
northlake.how_to_check_line: The City of Northlake Lead Safe Community hub (lead-norlkpw.hub.arcgis.com) has a "Lead Service Line Map" (searchable inventory) and a "Water Service Line Material Survey" (Survey123 form) residents fill out about their home's service line material. The city's older lead page also provided a self-inspection brochure/form (scratch the pipe with a screwdriver/sandpaper to identify material).
northlake.how_to_apply: No published application form. The program is city-driven: replacements are done via the city's inventory and water main replacement projects. Contact: City of Northlake Public Works Department, 100 W. Palmer, Northlake, IL 60164, phone 708-562-0940 (contact listed on the Lead Safe Community hub).
northlake.notes: Scale and pace per official city sources: ~20% of residential water services are lead; city estimated ~3,000 service lines with potentially ~600 lead lines at $6-8 million total. Replaced 81 lead services in 2024 (~$600,000); goal 100 in 2025 and 200 in 2026. Since 2021, lead services are replaced whenever encountered during water main replacement projects (e.g., 11 lead services replaced with the 100 block of N. Roy Avenue main in 2025). City states all lead/galvanized lines must be replaced by 2042 under Public Act 102-0613 (IL Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act) and that it is on track to finish well ahead of the deadline (earlier city page cited ~2035 if pace maintained); city says it will pursue grant funding to accelerate. Caveat: the city's dedicated page northlakecity.com/lead-water-service-line/ currently returns 404 after a site redesign — its quoted statements come from search-engine indexed text of that official URL; current live official info is on the public-works/about page, the Lead Safe Community ArcGIS hub, city news articles, and city newsletters. A "2024 Lead Service Line Inventory and Replacement Plan" PDF existed on the old site but the URL is now dead.

oak-forest.water_system: City of Oak Forest operates its own water distribution system (IL0312190); water is Lake Michigan water purchased from the Village of Oak Lawn (originating via the City of Chicago, treated at Chicago's Jardine Water Purification Plant)
oak-forest.cost_coverage: not published — the official page states only that under the Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act (Public Act 102-0613) "The City of Oak Forest will be required to replace between 5% to 7% of the lead service lines annually" and that "The City will be required to prepare a lead service line replacement program for the community, but this effort will require resident cooperation." The Act requires replacement of lead service lines from the watermain to the water meter in the home. No statement on who pays or whether the city covers the private portion.
oak-forest.how_to_check_line: Official self-inspection instructions on the city's Lead Service Line Questionnaire page (or hire a licensed plumber), then report the material via the city's online Survey123 questionnaire (https://survey123.arcgis.com/share/07bc9b56f0524d7bb8e6131de8544779?portalUrl=https://gismaps.hrgreen.com/portal). No public inventory map/portal for looking up an address is published.
oak-forest.how_to_apply: not published — no application process exists yet; the city is still in the inventory phase. Contact: Public Works Water Operator Mike Bjelke, mbjelke@oak-forest.org, 708-535-4090.
oak-forest.notes: Oak Forest is currently in the inventory/questionnaire stage, not an active replacement program: the city says it "will be required to prepare a lead service line replacement program" and is asking residents to self-identify their service line material (homes built before 1986 may have lead). No timeline, cost coverage, waitlist, loan program, or coordination with water-main projects is published on official pages. Water is Lake Michigan water purchased wholesale from Oak Lawn (Chicago-treated), but Oak Forest runs its own distribution system, so Oak Forest's (future) program is the applicable one for residents.

oak-lawn.water_system: Village of Oak Lawn operates its own Water Division and is a Lake Michigan water supplier — the official Public Works page states Oak Lawn "provides water to neighboring communities, making the Village of Oak Lawn the 2nd largest user/supplier of Lake Michigan water."
oak-lawn.cost_coverage: Not published. The village page states only: "With funding anticipated to be provided by the Illinois Public Water Supply Loan program, we will soon be able to start Phase 1." No language on who pays for the public vs. private portion or homeowner cost appears on the official pages.
oak-lawn.how_to_check_line: not published (no inventory map/portal is posted; per IEPA requirements the village mailed notices to all property owners with potential lead, galvanized, or unknown service lines — residents with questions are directed to the Water Division at (708) 499-7747)
oak-lawn.how_to_apply: not published — no application/enrollment process is described; contact the Water Division at (708) 499-7747. The village says the deployment plan, an extensive FAQ list, what to expect during replacement, and public meeting dates "will be posted in the next few weeks."
oak-lawn.notes: Village plans to replace approximately 2,300 lead and galvanized service lines over the next 5 years, funded (anticipated) by the Illinois Public Water Supply Loan program. Phase 1 prioritizes "preschool, medical, and other care facilities"; the Village Board will select a contractor to complete the work. Coordination with water-main projects is not addressed on official pages. Program details (deployment plan, FAQs, meetings) were stated as forthcoming, so cost/enrollment specifics may be published soon — the (708) 499-7747 Water Division line is the authoritative contact.

oak-park.water_system: Village of Oak Park operates its own community water system; per the Village's official FAQ, "The Village purchases Lake Michigan water from the City of Chicago. Water arrives pretreated via pipelines from the City of Chicago's Jardine Water Purification Plant."
oak-park.program_name: Two named village programs on the official site: "Lead Abatement Program" (public-side replacement) and "Lead Water Service Replacement Grant" (income-qualified full replacement, CDBG-funded); overall planning under the Village's Lead Service Line Replacement Plan (draft submitted April 2024, final due by 2027)
oak-park.cost_coverage: Village pays only the public side by default: per the official FAQ, "The Village will change the service line from the shutoff valve in the parkway to the Village's water main if needed, and restore the pavement at no cost to the resident," while "Property owners are responsible for the cost of replacing the service line from the shutoff valve in the parkway to the house" (no dollar figure is published). Under the Lead Abatement Program — which applies to residential properties with lead service lines in the Village right-of-way, up to 2-inch diameter (commercial properties do not qualify) — "the Village will construct, at no expense to the property owner, a new 1 inch water service, or equivalent size of existing, from the watermain up to and including a new B-Box to be located in the parkway." The owner pays the material cost of any upsizing beyond a 1-inch (or existing-size) line; and if the owner requests a new service where the existing line already meets minimum standards, the owner pays the full installation up to the water main (including the Village's tap fee and disconnection of the old service) plus any street, curb, sidewalk, and parkway restoration. Separately, the Lead Water Service Replacement Grant (HUD CDBG-funded) offers replacement with "no cost to participate in the program for those who qualify" — household income limits apply — but that grant program is listed as paused for the 2026 project year.
oak-park.homeowner_cost: Per the official FAQ: "Property owners are responsible for the cost of replacing the service line from the shutoff valve in the parkway to the house." No dollar figure is published. Income-qualified owners can get it free via the (currently paused) CDBG grant program. Under the Abatement Program the owner pays the material cost of any upsizing beyond a 1-inch (or existing-size) line; an owner who requests a new service where the existing line already meets minimum standards pays the full installation up to the water main (including the Village's tap fee and disconnection of the old service) plus any street, curb, sidewalk, and parkway restoration.
oak-park.how_to_check_line: Official Water Service Line Material Inventory ArcGIS dashboard (https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/97cfcb6247a24abc9baf9f227fb21f55) linked from leadfreeoakpark.com/village-wide-inventory/; residents with unknown/incorrect data can complete the Village's Water Service Line Survey (Survey123: https://survey123.arcgis.com/share/aad14001d66b40bf8fa7c9c55650975e) or contact Public Works at 708-358-5700 / publicworks@oak-park.us to arrange an in-home inspection.
oak-park.how_to_apply: Lead Water Service Replacement Grant: 708.358.5413 or housing@oak-park.us (Neighborhood Services / housing programs). Lead Abatement Program and general LSLR questions: Public Works Department, 708.358.5700 or publicworks@oak-park.us.
oak-park.notes: Official info source is the Village's dedicated site leadfreeoakpark.com ("Oak Park Lead", Village of Oak Park logo/footer); the main oak-park.us pages returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching. Under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act, the Village submitted a draft LSLR plan in April 2024 and will submit a final plan by 2027, with annual notification to properties with identified lead lines; a draft 2026 plan submittal PDF exists at oak-park.us (lslr-plan-oak-park-draft-2026-submittal.pdf, not readable due to 403). The CDBG-funded free-replacement grant is "currently paused for the 2026 project year" per the site. In the grant program the Village hires and oversees the contractor and work is typically completed in one day. No loan program and no explicit water-main-project coordination policy is published on the official pages read. Replacement swaps lead/galvanized pipe for 1-inch copper.

orland-hills.water_system: Illinois American Water (private utility). The Village of Orland Hills' own website states: "Illinois American Water is your local water and wastewater company." The village itself publishes no lead service line program — Illinois American Water's statewide program applies.
orland-hills.program_name: Illinois American Water Lead Service Line Replacement Program (customer identification component branded "Pipe Up")
orland-hills.cost_coverage: No cost to the homeowner when the replacement is initiated/scheduled by Illinois American Water and the owner signs and returns the agreement allowing the contractor to work on the property — the company covers the full cost, including the homeowner-owned portion. Replacements are done only "as a programmed and planned activity" (prioritized alongside water-main replacement/rehabilitation/relocation projects), not upon individual request; if a homeowner replaces their line on their own ahead of the company's scheduled replacement, "costs will not be covered or reimbursed by Illinois American Water."
orland-hills.homeowner_cost: No cost when the replacement is company-initiated and the owner signs the agreement; homeowner bears full cost (no reimbursement) if they replace the line on their own outside the company's schedule.
orland-hills.how_to_check_line: Illinois American Water offers a "Lead Service Line Replacement Map" and a "Pipe Up" self-assessment tool on its Lead and Drinking Water page (amwater.com/ilaw) to identify service line material; material is verified via customer survey responses and visual field inspection. Customers can also call 1-800-422-2782.
orland-hills.how_to_apply: Replacement is not available on request — the company identifies and contacts qualifying properties. Customers can submit questions via the Lead Service Line Replacement Program contact form at amwater.com/ilaw (response in 1-3 business days) or call 1-800-422-2782; the property owner must sign an agreement before the homeowner-portion replacement proceeds.
orland-hills.notes: Replacements are prioritized in conjunction with water main replacement, rehabilitation, relocation, and scheduled meter change work, using a company prioritization model weighing likelihood of lead, number of affected properties, proximity to schools/critical facilities, coordination with other infrastructure work, and census vulnerability data; affected customers receive advance notification before work in their area. Orland Hills is in Illinois American Water's Northern Division. No Orland Hills-specific lead service line inventory count, timeline, or waitlist is published on either the village or utility site. No village-funded program exists since the village does not own the water system.

orland-park.water_system: Village of Orland Park owns and operates its own distribution system (main pumping station, seven elevated tanks, three booster stations); water is supplied by the Village of Oak Lawn, which purchases Lake Michigan water from the Chicago Department of Water Management. Exception per the official plan: "in the Orland Ridge subdivision, water is supplied by Illinois American Water."
orland-park.program_name: not named (official document is the "Village of Orland Park Draft Lead Service Line Replacement Plan," July 2024, prepared by Baxter & Woodman, IEPA system IL0312310)
orland-park.cost_coverage: not published (plan says the Village "is assessing what funding programs and local revenue sources will minimize the debt service and overall financial impact on the Village and its consumers"; a cost-share program is only listed as a possibility)
orland-park.homeowner_cost: not published (plan says the Village "is assessing what funding programs and local revenue sources will minimize the debt service and overall financial impact on the Village and its consumers"; a cost-share program is only listed as a possibility)
orland-park.how_to_check_line: The inventory is complete: the Village "has identified the material of all 24,260 water service lines" (0 unknowns as of Feb 2024) — 4 lead and 14 galvanized steel, all on the private side; Village side is 100% copper without lead solder. Appendix A of the draft plan is a "Village of Orland Park Water Service Line Material Map." No public lookup portal is published; the Water & Utilities page links a "Lead Brochure" and the draft replacement plan, and Public Works can be reached at (708) 403-6350 or publicworks@orlandpark.org.
orland-park.how_to_apply: No application/signup program is published (only 4 lead + 14 galvanized lines village-wide; the Village initiates replacements with 45-day written notice to affected owners). A property owner initiating their own replacement must notify the Village at least 45 days before work and obtain a permit "through the Village's Citizen Services portal or by contacting the Village's Community Development Department." General lead questions: Public Works, (708) 403-6350.
orland-park.notes: Timeline per the official draft plan: mandatory replacements begin 2027 at Illinois' 7% annual rate (minimum 2 lines/year), with all 18 lead/GRR lines scheduled to be replaced by 2036 (statutory deadline 2042). None of the Village's 170 high-risk facilities (schools, daycares, medical) has a lead line. Lead sampling at ~60 sites shows 90th percentile of ~1 ppb, well under the 15 ppb action level; page states lead "has not, and is not, currently found within the drinking water supply." Village provides NSF/ANSI 53+42 filters at time of any replacement and offers follow-up lead sampling within 3-6 months; partial replacements prohibited unless owner denies access (owner must then sign IDPH waiver). Plan notes the Village "may coordinate lead and GRR water service line replacements" with future CIP (water main) projects. Access note: orlandpark.org blocks automated fetchers (Akamai 403); content was read from Wayback Machine captures of the official Water & Utilities page (Jan 2026) and the official Draft LSLR Plan PDF hosted on orlandpark.org (July 2025 capture of the July 2024 plan) — data (e.g., "4 lead lines") may since have been updated.

palatine.water_system: Village of Palatine operates its own water system (Water Division, 301+ miles of mains); drinking water is Lake Michigan water supplied via the Evanston Treatment Facility and the Northwest Water Commission
palatine.program_name: Lead and Galvanized Steel Water Service Line Replacement Cost Sharing Program
palatine.cost_coverage: Per the official village page: the Village reimburses "100% of the cost to replace the lead or galvanized steel service line from the water main to the water shut off valve (b-box)" and "3/4 of the cost from the b-box to the meter, up to a $11,000 maximum reimbursement." Permit and inspection fees are paid upfront by the resident/applicant but are reimbursable in addition to the $11,000 cap (they do not count against it). The $11,000 cap applies to the combined total reimbursement (public plus private segments). Participation is voluntary and open to all residential properties with an existing lead or galvanized steel water service line.
palatine.homeowner_cost: Homeowner pays 1/4 of the cost of the private segment (b-box to meter) plus any amount exceeding the $11,000 village reimbursement cap; the public segment (main to b-box) is reimbursed at 100%. Homeowner hires their own licensed, bonded plumbing contractor.
palatine.how_to_check_line: Official inventory GIS dashboard (linked from palatine.il.us/883): https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/248b80540e7e468aa3b924e25bb4b6a7 — look up your address with the map's search tool. Alternatively do a scratch test at the water meter (copper = penny-colored/non-magnetic; lead = shiny silver/non-magnetic; galvanized = dull gray/magnetic). If unsure, email photos of the meter/piping to publicworks@palatine.il.us for review by the Engineering Division.
palatine.how_to_apply: Contact the Department of Public Works Engineering Division at (847) 705-5200 or publicworks@palatine.il.us; complete and submit the program application form (available at palatine.il.us/DocumentCenter/View/3072) for pre-approval of the reimbursement amount BEFORE applying for a building permit.
palatine.notes: Reimbursement model: homeowner selects and hires a plumbing contractor licensed and bonded to work in the Village of Palatine; contractor must restore public property to pre-construction condition. Lead/galvanized lines qualify equally. Village inventory data was gathered largely during the 2015 water meter replacement project and feeds the public GIS dashboard. Timelines, waitlists, and any water-main-project-driven scheduling: not published on the official pages read. An IEPA Funding Notice page also exists (palatine.il.us/949) suggesting state loan/grant funding involvement, but it was not read in detail.

palos-park.water_system: Village of Palos Park operates its own community water supply (IEPA ID IL0311000). Per the 2024 CCR: Lake Michigan water treated by the City of Chicago Water Department, pumped to the Oak Lawn Water System; Oak Lawn pumps it to a Village reservoir and pumping station in Palos Park, where the Village adds chlorine and distributes to customers.
palos-park.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's 2024 Annual Water Quality Report states: "In 2024, the Village of Palos Park submitted its Lead Service Inventory to the Illinois EPA, in which it was found that the village does not have any known Lead service lines." With no known lead lines, no replacement/cost-coverage program is described.
palos-park.homeowner_cost: not published (no replacement program described; village reports no known lead service lines)
palos-park.how_to_check_line: The Lead Service Line Inventory is available to the public on request: "To request a copy of either of these documents, please contact Daniel Foster at 708-671-3722" (Daniel Foster, Utility Department Supervisor). Residents concerned about lead can also have water tested — "contact the Village of Palos Park at 708-671-3722." No online inventory map/portal published.
palos-park.how_to_apply: not published (no program to apply to; utility contact is Daniel Foster, Utility Department Supervisor, 708-671-3722)
palos-park.notes: Official source is the Village's 2024 Annual Water Quality Report (CCR), mailed to residents and hosted on palospark.org. The Village complied with the Illinois LSLRNA by submitting its service line inventory to Illinois EPA in 2024 and reports ZERO known lead service lines, so unlike many Chicago suburbs there is no village-funded replacement program, waitlist, or water-main-coordinated replacement schedule. 2024 lead 90th-percentile sampling result was 4.3 ug/L (action level 15), 0 sites over AL, no violation. No dedicated lead-service-line page was found on palospark.org beyond the CCR; inventory copies are provided on request by phone.

park-forest.water_system: The Village of Park Forest operates its own municipal water system, supplied by groundwater from six wells (~300 ft deep, dolomite limestone aquifer) within a one-mile radius of the Village Water Plant; treatment includes lime/soda-ash softening, filtration, chlorination, orthophosphate corrosion control, and fluoridation.
park-forest.cost_coverage: not published — the Village's lead service line page covers only the inventory/survey stage required by Illinois Public Act 102-0613 (Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act) and states no replacement funding or cost-sharing terms. The page does state line ownership: "Water service lines from the public water main, up to and including the exterior water shut off valve/buffalo box, are owned and maintained by the Village"; the owner maintains the line from that valve into the building.
park-forest.how_to_check_line: Official self-check instructions on the Village's "Lead Pipe Self-Service" page: locate the pipe entering the water meter, scratch it with a key/coin and apply a magnet (copper = penny color, no magnet; lead = shiny silver, possible bulb joint, no magnet; galvanized steel = dull gray, magnet sticks), then report the result via the Village's online Google Form survey. Alternatively, residents can book a ~5-minute inspection appointment (Lead Service Line Appointments) or call the Department of Public Works at 708-503-7702; the Village is surveying all homes and businesses and mailed letters requesting appointments. No public inventory map/portal is published.
park-forest.how_to_apply: not published — no replacement program application exists; for service-line identification contact the Department of Public Works, 708-503-7702, or use the Village's online appointment/self-survey links.
park-forest.notes: Park Forest is still in the service-line material inventory phase under Illinois PA 102-0613; the Village states homes were generally built with copper service lines but some may contain lead or lead components. No replacement schedule, funding source, waitlist, loan program, or water-main-project coordination is published on official Village pages. Caution for content writing: search results are heavily polluted by the separate Village of Forest Park, IL (forestpark.net), which does have an IEPA-funded replacement program — do not conflate the two. Village Hall: 350 Victory Drive, Park Forest, IL 60466, 708-748-1112. Water rates FY2025-26: $21.95 per 1,000 gallons.

park-ridge.water_system: City of Park Ridge operates its own water distribution system; per the official page, "The City receives treated drinking water from Lake Michigan from the City of Chicago."
park-ridge.cost_coverage: not published — the official page states only the ownership split: "the City of Park Ridge service line is owned partially by the City (Water Main up to and including the B-box) and partially by the property owner (B-box to the Water Meter)." It states the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act (effective Jan 1, 2022) requires all lead service lines to be replaced, with a Park Ridge deadline of 2044, but says nothing about who pays for the replacements.
park-ridge.how_to_check_line: Official "Lead Service Inventory Public Dashboard" (ArcGIS) linked from the city's Lead Service Line page: https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/a57a8ff8ef9b482e806e039b86d7ec53 — residents can look up their service line material classification. The city states the material inventory (public and private portions) is underway per the 2027 inventory requirement, and "All residents with service lines identified as lead have been notified."
park-ridge.how_to_apply: not published — no application process or dedicated program contact on the official page; only the general city number 847-318-5200 (M-F 8am-5pm) and the Public Works water quality pages.
park-ridge.notes: Official timeline: inventory by 2027, all lead lines replaced by 2044 (per the state Act). The city's construction projects page says the City replaces 1-2 blocks of water main per year and that such projects include "new services up to and including a new shut-off," but does not explicitly tie this to lead service line replacement or state who pays. No official page describes a formal replacement program, funding assistance, or loan program; a news outlet reported the city was applying for an IEPA 0% loan to cover replacements without homeowner cost, but this is NOT confirmed on any official city page and is excluded per instructions.

port-barrington.water_system: No municipal/community water system. Residents use individual private wells — the Village's own site states "McHenry County Department of Health and Lake County Health Department are offering reduced fee water testing for individual well users" and encourages residents to test well water annually for coliform bacteria and nitrates. The Village has no water department or water utility pages; it only handles stormwater management.
port-barrington.cost_coverage: not published — no official Port Barrington page on lead service lines exists; since residents are on private wells there is no village water system subject to the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act
port-barrington.how_to_check_line: not published — no service line inventory exists for Port Barrington because there is no community water supply; village site directs well owners to county health department water testing (sampling kits available at Village Hall, 69 S. Circle Ave., 847-639-7595)
port-barrington.how_to_apply: not published — no program exists; general water questions go to Village Hall, villagehall@portbarrington.net, (847) 639-7595
port-barrington.notes: Do not confuse with the separate Village of Barrington, IL (barrington-il.gov), which does have an LSLR program with IEPA grant funding — search results are dominated by it, but it does not serve Port Barrington. Port Barrington official pages read: home page, water testing kits page, stormwater management page — none mention lead or service lines; the water-testing page refers to "individual well users" served by McHenry and Lake County health departments (McHenry County well test: $30 coliform/E.coli plus nitrate screen). found_official_info is false only in the strict sense that no official lead-service-line page exists to read; official village pages confirming private-well supply were read.

prospect-heights.water_system: Split system: the City of Prospect Heights operates a small municipal water system (~494 service connections per its inventory; earlier city studies cite ~1,080 connections serving ~2,700 people in the Rob Roy development, Camp McDonald Rd, Wheeling Rd, Casa Court, and Lake Claire areas) supplied with Lake Michigan water purchased through two connections with Illinois-American Water Company. The majority of properties in the city are NOT on city water — they use private wells, which the city does not regulate.
prospect-heights.cost_coverage: not published — no replacement program exists because the city's official IEPA Lead Service Line Inventory (Water System ID IL0312530, current inventory date Feb 2024) reports "Total Service lines: 494, Total Lead: 0, Total Non-Lead: 494, Total Galvanized Requiring replacement: 0, Total Unknown: 0". Every entry in the address-level inventory is classified Non-Lead (materials are copper, copper with lead solder, and one "Unknown Not Lead").
prospect-heights.homeowner_cost: not published (not applicable — zero lead service lines in the official inventory)
prospect-heights.how_to_check_line: The city's official Water page (prospect-heights.il.us/121/Water) posts a downloadable "Water Service Line Inventory" spreadsheet (DocumentCenter/View/3822) listing every service address with PWS-side and customer-side material, plus a "Property Potable Water Source Map" (DocumentCenter/View/3825) showing which properties are on city water vs private wells.
prospect-heights.how_to_apply: not published (no program). General water/utility contact on the official page: Utility Billing, 847-398-6070 Ext. 214, finance@prospect-heights.org.
prospect-heights.notes: The official Water page also shows Lead Tap Sample Data 2008-2023 with zero sites exceeding the 15 ppb action level, and links residents with lead concerns to Cook County DPH and Illinois EPA resources. Because the city's inventory shows no lead, galvanized-requiring-replacement, or unknown lines, no LSLR plan/waitlist/main-project coordination is published. Note: 229 of 495 inventoried lines are copper with lead solder (CLS), which counts as Non-Lead under the Act. Properties on private wells fall outside any community-water-system inventory; homeowners there are responsible for their own wells per the city site. Illinois-American Water is only the wholesale supplier to the city system, so its LSLR program does not apply to Prospect Heights city-water customers.

river-forest.water_system: Village of River Forest owns/operates its own community water supply; Lake Michigan water treated at Chicago's treatment plant, then piped to the Village's Pumping Station where additional chlorine is added before distribution.
river-forest.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Program — resident assistance component branded "Get the Lead Out" Resident Assistance Program (reimbursement program, Revised June 2024)
river-forest.cost_coverage: Homeowner hires and pays the plumbing contractor up front and is reimbursed by the Village only after all work is completed, inspected, and approved: 100% of Village-portion costs (water main to buffalo box) up to $5,000 and 50% of private-portion costs (buffalo box to water meter) up to $2,500, with total reimbursement capped at $7,500 unless otherwise approved by Village Staff. Reimbursement is calculated from the lowest of the three required contractor estimates regardless of which contractor is selected, so choosing a higher bid increases the homeowner's out-of-pocket share. Homeowner bears: the other 50% of private-side costs and anything above the caps; the replacement cost of any non-lead piping; cost increases from installing a water service larger than the required minimum (1-1/2" in the right-of-way; 1" on the private side, or larger based on fixture count); removal/replacement of interior walls and finishes; landscaping and excavation restoration beyond program limits (32 sq ft); restoration of landscaping and correction of subsidence on private property; and future maintenance from the buffalo box to the water meter. Private-side replacement is recommended but not mandatory; if a leak occurs on the private portion, immediate repair is required but full copper replacement is still only recommended. For the separate IEPA-driven village-initiated replacement program, homeowner cost "has not yet been determined" and "may be dictated by the funding sources."
river-forest.homeowner_cost: Homeowner hires and pays the plumbing contractor up front and is reimbursed only after all work is completed, inspected, and approved: 100% of Village-portion costs up to $5,000 and 50% of private-portion costs up to $2,500 (total cap $7,500 unless otherwise approved by Village Staff), with reimbursement calculated from the lowest of the three required contractor estimates regardless of which contractor is selected. Homeowner bears: the other 50% of private-side costs and anything above the caps, replacement of non-lead piping, cost increases from installing a water service larger than the required minimum (1-1/2" in the right-of-way; 1" on the private side, or larger based on fixture count), removal/replacement of interior walls and finishes, landscaping beyond program limits, private-property restoration/subsidence, and future maintenance from buffalo box to meter. For the separate IEPA-driven village-initiated replacement program, homeowner cost "has not yet been determined" and "may be dictated by the funding sources."
river-forest.how_to_check_line: Two official options on vrf.us/leadsurvey: (1) submit a photo survey (contact info plus two photos of the water service/meter, from 2 ft and 10 ft) at https://survey123.arcgis.com/share/630d1ae3c26d40dc941f1df7181244e8; (2) view the interactive ArcGIS dashboard map of known service line materials at https://www.arcgis.com/apps/dashboards/a2df30b07e374a9c8565440d6173ce88. Village staff site inspections are also available for properties impacted by projects.
river-forest.how_to_apply: Obtain at least 3 contractor estimates; complete the Reimbursement Program Application Form and Property Owner Participation Agreement (in the Get the Lead Out packet at vrf.us); submit a single full permit package (application, agreement, itemized estimate separating Village and owner portions, scope description, site plan, Water Service Sizing Detail) through the Village's online permit portal at https://riverforest.onlama.com using permit type "Plumbing with Digging". Program is administered by Public Works (Public Works Director, 400 Park Avenue, River Forest, IL 60305; 708-366-8500). After completion and approved inspections, submit the Request for Reimbursement Form; reimbursements typically issued and mailed within 2-4 weeks.
river-forest.notes: LSLR Program approved by Village Board May 2021. Program is not retroactive — work started before Village approval is not reimbursable; one reimbursement per property; all lead portions must be replaced at the same time; 1-1/2" Type K copper (or other IEPA-approved material) basis; 3-year warranty on labor and materials required; directional drilling through the public right-of-way unless otherwise approved. Separate from the reimbursement program, the Village is developing an IEPA-mandated inventory and replacement plan; residents receive notice by mail 45 days prior to scheduled replacement work, and the Village replaces its portion with copper during water main projects. The Village states it "will continue to pursue all funding opportunities available for this work" (state/federal grants and loans); no village loan program is published. No published waitlist.

river-grove.water_system: Village of River Grove operates its own municipal water system (River Grove Public Works / Water Department); the official page states "The Village of River Grove receives drinking water from Lake Michigan." The wholesale supplier of the Lake Michigan water is not published on the pages read.
river-grove.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement Program (also referred to in construction notices as the "Village's Lead Water Service Replacement Program")
river-grove.cost_coverage: $0 for homes within the Village's 2025 Water Main Improvements project area (River Rd from Kennedy Ave to Belmont Ave, Belmont Ave from Elm St to River Rd, and Elm St from Walnut Ave to Belmont Ave): the official September 12, 2025 construction notice states existing lead water service pipes "will be replaced from the water main to the water meter located inside of your home as part of the Village's Lead Water Service Replacement Program, at no cost to you," and Brita filters are available for pickup at no cost for the recommended 6 months of post-replacement filter use. Outside such project areas, the private portion (past the curb box) is the property owner's expense; the Village LSL page cites replacement costs of "$6,000 to $16,000" per line and says the Village "intends to apply for significant state and/or federal funding to offset the cost of private lead service line replacement" (an intention, not a commitment). The Village also charges a water-rate component of $2.70 per 1,000 gallons toward the program, versus a $6.93 per 1,000 gallons rate the page says full replacement cost would require. No income limits or caps are stated on either page.
river-grove.homeowner_cost: $0 for homes within a Village water-main improvement project area (full replacement main-to-meter "at no cost to you", plus free Brita filters for 6 months post-replacement). Outside such projects, the private portion is the owner's expense; the LSL page cites replacement costs of "$6,000 to $16,000" per line. The Village also adopted a water-rate component ($2.70 per 1,000 gallons, vs. $6.93 full-cost rate) to help fund the program.
river-grove.how_to_check_line: The Village publishes a Water Service Line Material Inventory (searchable by address) linked from the Lead Service Line Replacement page (latest: "RiverGrove IL0312640 IEPA 2026 Final Material Inventory" PDF at rivergroveil.gov/DocumentCenter/View/3495). The page also provides pipe self-identification instructions. Notices were mailed in January 2023 to owners/residents of buildings identified with lead service.
river-grove.how_to_apply: No application form published. Replacement is project-driven: during water-main projects, the contractor (2025: Acqua Contractors Corp.) contacts affected homes to schedule an interior inspection and then installation. General program questions: Water Department 708-453-8000 (press 4); Public Works Director Brock Leder 708-452-7055, bleder@rivergroveil.gov.
river-grove.notes: River Grove has 1,881 lead/galvanized service lines with an estimated $28.3 million total replacement cost; state/federal mandate requires all replaced by 2044. Replacement is being scheduled with annual water-main improvement projects (2025 project covered River Rd from Kennedy to Belmont, Belmont Ave from Elm to River Rd, and Elm St from Walnut to Belmont; completed ~Dec 2025). The village page also says that if the Village later replaces the b-box-to-main portion, it "is willing to coordinate with homeowners to replace the remaining portion." Free Brita filters for 6 months after replacement are available at Public Works, 2101 West St. No waitlist or standalone (non-project) village-funded private replacement is published.

riverdale.water_system: Village of Riverdale operates its own community water system (Illinois EPA PWS ID IL0312580, ~10,266 residents, 3,311 metered connections) and purchases Lake Michigan water from the City of Chicago (seller PWS IL0316000) per Illinois EPA Drinking Water Watch. Because Riverdale owns its distribution system, Riverdale — not Chicago — is the responsible community water supply under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act; Chicago's LSL program does not apply to Riverdale residents.
riverdale.cost_coverage: not published — the Village of Riverdale's official website (villageofriverdale.net) has no lead service line page or any statement about who pays for replacements
riverdale.how_to_check_line: not published — no inventory map or lookup portal found on the village website or Illinois EPA's public pages. Illinois EPA directs inventory inquiries to EPA.LeadandCopper@illinois.gov or (217) 785-0561; residents can also contact Riverdale Public Works, 157 W. 144th St, Riverdale, IL 60827
riverdale.how_to_apply: not published — no program or application exists on official pages; the relevant department would be Riverdale Public Works (maintains the water and sewer systems per villageofriverdale.net)
riverdale.notes: The official village site (villageofriverdale.net) publishes no lead service line inventory, replacement plan, or cost-sharing policy; a site-wide search found no mention of lead service lines in any page, agenda, or minutes. The only water documents on the Public Works page are a 2018 Consumer Confidence Report (scanned image PDF, not machine-readable) and a water-saving-tips flyer. Riverdale does not appear in the Illinois EPA FY2026 Public Water Supply Loan Program Intended Use Plan (searched full PDF text), so no state lead-service-line replacement loan project is currently listed for it. As an Illinois community water supply, Riverdale is subject to the LSLRNA inventory/replacement mandates, but nothing about its compliance status is published on official pages. Note: villageofriverdale.org is an unrelated/squatted domain; the official site is villageofriverdale.net.

riverside.water_system: Village of Riverside operates its own distribution system; official Water & Sewer page states "The Village of Riverside purchases its water from the city of Chicago and distributes it throughout the village using a pump system." (IEPA facility ID IL-0312670)
riverside.program_name: not named (village pages call it "Lead Service Line Replacement" under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act, Public Act 102-0613)
riverside.cost_coverage: not published (no homeowner charge is stated on the official Lead Service Line Replacement page or in the 2025 LSLR Plan cost tables, which budget the private portion — including a "PRIVATE WATER SERVICE LINE, 1 INCH COPPER" item at $8,000 x 1,765 plus private foundation and meter connections — within the village's $32,375,750 program; the only identified funding is a $12,000,000 PWSLP/SRF loan, covering part of the estimate. The village page describes the SRF-financed project as replacing lines "from the buffalo box to the meter", i.e., the private side, with public-side items also budgeted in the plan)
riverside.homeowner_cost: not published (no homeowner charge is stated on the official Lead Service Line Replacement page or in the 2025 LSLR Plan cost tables, which budget the private portion within village/SRF funding)
riverside.how_to_check_line: Official "Lead Service Inventory Dashboard" (ArcGIS map) linked from https://www.riverside.il.us/726/Lead-Service-Line-Replacement; if a resident believes their address is listed in error, contact Public Works at 708-442-3590
riverside.how_to_apply: not published as an application process — replacements are scheduled by the village (2025 Capital Improvement Projects Map shows current replacement locations); contact Public Works at 708-442-3590; residents can subscribe to E-Flash construction updates via the village's "Let's Keep in Touch" page
riverside.notes: Official plan data (Appendix B): 3,031 total services, 1,765 lead services, 10% goal / minimum 177 replacements per year (5.8% annual ratio), 15-year schedule, plan completion 2042; the village webpage says it "anticipates completing the State required deadline by 2044." Village states it "does not have any reported issues of lead in the drinking water." Plan includes a lead filter pitcher with six months of cartridges per replaced service and a High Risk Facilities Priority Plan (e.g., 3200 Harlem). IEPA notice templates in the plan reference water-main-replacement-coordinated service line work, consistent with replacements tied to water main projects. Local news (Riverside-Brookfield Landmark, Feb 2026 — NOT an official source, excluded from official fields) reported the board approved reimbursing the public-portion cost ($5,000 same-side / $7,500 opposite-side caps) for homeowners replacing early; no official village page confirming this was found, so it is treated as not published. Note: North Riverside, IL is a separate municipality with its own LSLR page.

riverwoods.water_system: Village of Riverwoods operates its own municipal water system serving the majority of residents; per the Village's official Water Quality Consumer Confidence Report page, the source is surface water purchased from the Village of Northbrook (Lake Michigan), drawn into a 1-million-gallon ground storage reservoir and pumped into the Riverwoods distribution system. Some residents remain on private wells (annual well test required by the Village).
riverwoods.cost_coverage: not published — the Village of Riverwoods website has no lead service line replacement page; a site-restricted search of riverwoods.gov returns no lead service line content, and the official Utilities & Services page (read in full via a Feb 2025 archived copy; the live site blocks automated access with Cloudflare) covers only water billing, sewer, and utility providers with no mention of lead pipes or a replacement program.
riverwoods.how_to_check_line: not published — no service line material inventory map or lookup portal was found on riverwoods.gov. The Illinois EPA's Lead Service Line Information page (read) describes the statewide LSLRNA inventory requirement generally but does not publish a Riverwoods-specific inventory lookup; its Community Updates page covers only Elgin. Residents would need to contact Riverwoods Village Hall, (847) 945-3990.
riverwoods.how_to_apply: not published — no program or application process appears on official pages. Water/utility questions go to Riverwoods Village Hall, 300 Portwine Rd., Riverwoods, IL 60015, (847) 945-3990; the Village's consulting engineer is Gewalt Hamilton Associates (utilities contact listed on riverwoods.gov: Kevin Tenney, ktenney@gha-engineers.com, 224-352-2706).
riverwoods.notes: Riverwoods is a small Lake County village (pop. ~3,700) that buys Lake Michigan water wholesale from Northbrook but runs its own distribution system, so under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act the Riverwoods system is responsible for its own inventory/replacement plan — yet no LSL inventory, replacement plan, or cost-coverage policy is published anywhere on riverwoods.gov. Caveats on research method: live riverwoods.gov pages return HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to all automated fetchers; the Utilities & Services page was read in full from a Feb 18, 2025 Wayback Machine capture of the official site, and Consumer Confidence Report page content (water source description) comes from search-engine excerpts of the official riverwoods.gov CCR page. It is possible LSL inventory details exist only inside board-meeting packet PDFs (also blocked) or the paper CCR, which the Village says can be picked up at Village Hall or at Gewalt Hamilton Associates' office. Statewide LSLRNA context: complete material inventories were due to Illinois EPA by April 15, 2024.

rolling-meadows.water_system: City of Rolling Meadows operates its own water system ("Approximately 1 billion gallons of Lake Michigan and well water is pumped yearly"). The city's Lead FAQ states "The City purchases its drinking water from the City of Chicago via NSM-JAWA," while the inventory page also references groundwater as source water — official pages describe a mix of Lake Michigan (Chicago via NSM-JAWA) and well water.
rolling-meadows.program_name: not named (only a "Lead Service Line Replacement Plan (Draft)" document is referenced; program is the "Lead Service Line Inventory Program")
rolling-meadows.cost_coverage: not published (ownership split implies homeowner responsibility for the private portion from the B-Box into the house, but no cost figures are stated)
rolling-meadows.homeowner_cost: not published (ownership split implies homeowner responsibility for the private portion from the B-Box into the house, but no cost figures are stated)
rolling-meadows.how_to_check_line: Interactive service line inventory map on the city's Lead Service Line Inventory Program page ("Click on the map below to review the City's current inventory of water service lines") showing known material on both public and private sides; residents with missing/unknown info can self-report via the City's Water Service Line Survey. FAQ also gives DIY checks (scratch test — lead "shines brightly when scratched"; magnet will not cling to lead).
rolling-meadows.how_to_apply: No application process published (no replacement program to apply to). Questions/reports go to Rolling Meadows Public Works: 847-963-0500 (ext. 7022 for the service line program), PW@cityrm.org, 3900 Berdnick Street, Rolling Meadows, IL 60008, M-F 7:00 a.m.-3:30 p.m.; or complete the online Water Service Line Survey.
rolling-meadows.notes: Key official statement: "There are no known lead service lines in Rolling Meadows" and the city is "in full compliance with the IEPA and USEPA"; "Lead is not present in the Rolling Meadows's source water... nor in water flowing through our distribution system." The city is still completing its Illinois LSLRNA-required inventory (415 ILCS 5/17.12, reporting deadline April 15, 2024) using online surveys, mailings, and in-person inspections to resolve unknown lines. A "Lead Service Line Replacement Plan (Draft)" document exists but no implementation details, timelines, or cost terms are published. Lead tap monitoring has run for 30+ years at 30 sites every three years; results well below the 15 ppb EPA action level as of 2023.

rosemont.water_system: Village of Rosemont operates its own community water supply (Public Works Water & Sewer Department, PWS ID IL0312760, ~363 residential and 371 commercial meters). Official water quality reports reference "sampling done by the City of Chicago" alongside the Village's own sampling, but the official pages read do not explicitly name the wholesale supplier/source.
rosemont.cost_coverage: not published — the July 15, 2025 Tier 1 Lead ALE public notice states "The Village will be replacing the remaining lead service lines this summer" and "We are removing the lead service lines... This work will be completed in the next 90 days," but says nothing about cost allocation between village and property owners
rosemont.how_to_check_line: No online lookup portal. The ALE notice says: "Contact us at 847 698-3744 or a licensed plumber to determine if the pipe that connects your home to the water main (called a service line) is made from lead, galvanized, or other materials." The village also publishes its full IEPA address-by-address material inventory PDF on the Water & Sewer page (rosemont.com/government/public-works/water-sewer/).
rosemont.how_to_apply: No application/form published. Per the ALE notice: "To find out about what we are doing to replace lead service lines, please contact us at 847 698-3744" (Village of Rosemont Public Works Department).
rosemont.notes: Rosemont exceeded the federal lead action level in H1 2025 (more than 10% of 40 samples over 15 ppb; Tier 1 public notice distributed 7/15/2025), which stated several lead service lines existed on the south side of the village and committed to replacing all remaining lead lines within 90 days (summer 2025). The subsequent IEPA Final Material Inventory dated 3/26/2026 shows the work is done: 734 total service lines, 0 lead, 0 galvanized-requiring-replacement, 0 unknown — 734 non-lead. Individual inventory rows show lead lines replaced between Feb 2023 and Oct 2025 (e.g., replacements dated 4/14/2025, 5/9/2024, 10/16-10/23/2025) at Chicago-addressed (60656) parcels served by the Rosemont system. So Rosemont's "program" was a village-driven full removal, now complete per official inventory — there is no ongoing application-based homeowner program, waitlist, or published loan/cost-share terms. Rosemont is a very small system; the ALE notice is a .docx and the inventory a PDF on the Water & Sewer page.

round-lake.water_system: Village of Round Lake operates its own water distribution system (community water supply IL0971500) serving ~18,721 customers with 5,368 service lines. Source water is pre-treated Lake Michigan water delivered via the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA), with a receiving station, 2 elevated tanks, a reservoir, and emergency stand-by wells.
round-lake.program_name: not named (official document is the "Village of Round Lake Draft Lead Service Line Replacement Plan," April 2024, prepared by Baxter & Woodman)
round-lake.cost_coverage: not published (cost-share terms undecided; plan cites an average full-replacement construction cost of $12,000-$15,000 per line in 2024 dollars for planning purposes only)
round-lake.homeowner_cost: not published (cost-share terms undecided; plan cites an average full-replacement construction cost of $12,000-$15,000 per line in 2024 dollars for planning purposes only)
round-lake.how_to_check_line: No online lookup portal is published. The Village Water page states the Public Works Department "keeps an inventory of confirmed and suspected lead service line locations" and "You can request a copy of this inventory from the Public Works Department" (847-546-0962). The draft plan's Appendix A contains a Village-wide service line material map; Figure 3 maps identified lead/galvanized locations (concentrated in the northeastern, oldest part of town).
round-lake.how_to_apply: No application process published. Contact the Public Works Department at 847-546-0962 (inventory requests, draft-plan comments, and required permits/45-day notice for owner-initiated service line replacement). Draft-plan comments may also be emailed to Public Works (address obfuscated on the site by email protection).
round-lake.notes: Small lead problem: of 5,368 service lines, 38 lead/GRR identified and 21 unknown as of the April 2024 draft plan (Village estimates ~40 total); 0 replaced through 2023; no lead lines at any of 20 identified high-risk facilities (one has unknown material, and any lead found there would be replaced by 2029). Timeline per Illinois Act: mandatory replacements begin 2027 at a 7% annual rate (minimum ~3 lines/year), full completion by 2041; final LSLR Plan due to IEPA April 15, 2027. Replacements will be executed within Capital Improvement Plan projects (e.g., water main projects) where possible plus a separate lead replacement program. Total estimated cost to replace all lines: ~$750,000; funding sources (federal/state/county loans-grants, water rates) still being assessed. If the Village disturbs a lead line during emergency work it must fully replace it within 30 days (120 in bad weather) and provide NSF-certified filters; property owners who deny access must sign an IDPH waiver, and rental/nonresidential owners who refuse must install point-of-use filters. Note: Round Lake (roundlakeil.gov) is distinct from neighboring Round Lake Beach (roundlakebeachil.gov), which ran its own door-to-door lead inventory survey completed Dec 31, 2024. Live roundlakeil.gov pages are behind a Cloudflare challenge; content verified via the March 2025 Wayback capture of the official pages.

schiller-park.water_system: Village of Schiller Park operates its own water system; per the Village's Water Quality Report, "The source of drinking water used by the Village is Purchased Surface Water from Lake Michigan through the City of Chicago." Water Superintendent: Pedro Sanchez, 847-671-8554.

schiller-park.homeowner_cost: not published (village page notes replacement cost "can be as much as $15,000" as a warning about opting out of the survey; the Grace Street project was TIF-funded with no homeowner charge stated)
