schiller-park.how_to_apply: not published (no application process exists; replacements so far are village-initiated with water-main projects). Contacts: Village Hall 847-678-2550; Public Works Director Patrick Hastings 847-671-8506; Water Superintendent Pedro Sanchez 847-671-8554.
schiller-park.notes: Village is in the inventory/funding-search phase under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act; the 2025 material inventory has been submitted to IEPA and is posted online. Replacement to date is project-driven: Grace Street lead services were replaced fall 2024 ahead of a 2025 TIF-funded water main project. A village "Lead Service Line Replacement FAQ" CivicAlert (AID 599) once existed but now returns 404. No timelines, waitlist, or village-wide cost-coverage commitment is published.

skokie.water_system: Village of Skokie operates its own distribution system; since 1944 Skokie has purchased its water from the City of Evanston (Lake Michigan water). The Village owns the public side (water main to Buffalo Box); the property owner owns the private side (Buffalo Box to water meter).
skokie.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Cost-Share Program (plus a separate Lead Service Line Rebate Program)
skokie.cost_coverage: Village pays for the public-side replacement; for the private side, "the Village's Lead Service Line Replacement program caps a private property owner's costs for the private side replacement of lead at $3,090 (adjustable annually as costs rise)." When Village projects (water main replacement, emergency repairs/leaks) trigger a replacement, the Village splits private-side costs 50/50 with the owner. The average private-side replacement alone costs approximately $6,000 through the Village's competitive bidding (vs. roughly $10,000 via a private plumber). Program expanded Dec 1, 2025 so households "will be able to self-select to participate in the cost-share program – even if they don't have a leak or a water main replacement project scheduled for their block," with projects scheduled as funding and resources permit and enrollment details promised by January 1, 2026. Homeowner cost: capped at $3,090 for the private-side replacement (adjustable annually as costs rise); payable all at once or via a "15-year payment plan at 1% interest" through the water bill. Separate rebate program: $750 or $1,250 water-bill credit for residential owners who already replaced their lead/galvanized line since January 2022, provided they document the replacement, are current on utility charges, and did not use the cost-share program.
skokie.homeowner_cost: Capped at $3,090 for the private-side replacement (adjustable annually as costs rise); financeable over 15 years through the water bill — the Village describes a "15-year payment plan at 1% interest" / "very low interest." Separate rebate program: $750 or $1,250 water-bill credit for owners who already replaced their line since January 2022.
skokie.how_to_check_line: Interactive service line inventory map at skokie.org/inventory, or a scratch-and-magnet test (screwdriver, sandpaper, refrigerator magnet) described on the Village's Lead Water Service Lines page.
skokie.how_to_apply: Complete the Village's LSLR Cost-Share Program interest form (online via skokie.org / CivicPlus form); residents who cannot access the online form may contact Skokie Public Works at 847-933-8427 to complete it by phone.
skokie.notes: Program expansion to self-selecting households approved by Village Board Dec 1, 2025; enrollment process details promised by Jan 1, 2026, with funding identified in the May 2026 budget process. Village plans 600+ service line replacements annually beginning in 2027 (ramping to 688/year per the expansion announcement), continuing 15+ years; projects scheduled to maximize replacements "as funding and resources permit" and coordinated with scheduled water main projects and emergency repairs.

south-barrington.water_system: Mostly private wells: per the Village website, "Groundwater supplies all of South Barrington residents' water needs, whether from a residential well or the Village's municipal water plant." Only three subdivisions (The Regency, Woods, and Village Enclave) have Village water/sewer service. The Village-owned system (Community Water Supply #IL0310200) is fed by two 1,300-ft-deep wells and is operated by Sheaffer & Roland Inc., Consulting Engineers (Geneva, IL). South Barrington is a separate municipality from the Village of Barrington, which has its own unrelated lead service line program.
south-barrington.cost_coverage: not published — official pages state no replacement program or cost-sharing terms. The 2025 CCR only includes the generic EPA statement: "The drinking water supplier is responsible for providing high quality drinking water and removing lead pipes, but cannot control the variety of materials used in plumbing components in your home."
south-barrington.how_to_check_line: Per the 2025 Annual Drinking Water Quality Report (published June 2026): "Our Community Water Supply has developed a service line material inventory. To obtain a copy of the system's service line inventory, please contact the District Operator at 630-208-9898." No online inventory map/portal is published.
south-barrington.how_to_apply: not published — no replacement program to apply to. Water service contacts: H2o@southbarrington.org (Village water/sewer services); District Operator (Sheaffer & Roland Inc.) 630-208-9898, after hours 630-675-9963; Village Hall (847) 381-7510 (questions on the water quality report go to Michael Dropka, Village Administrator).
south-barrington.notes: 2025 lead sampling: 90th percentile <1.0 ppb (range <1.0–3.5 ppb), 0 sites over the 15 ppb action level; no lead detected issues reported. Lead tap sampling data also available from the District Operator at 630-208-9898. The CCR notes one 2025 violation: the 2024 CCR was missing required language and copper range values in its lead/copper section (administrative, not a water-quality exceedance). Most South Barrington homes are on private wells/septic and are outside any community-water-system lead service line obligations; BACOG offers private well testing resources (bacog.org). No mention anywhere on official pages of lead service lines existing in the system, a replacement plan, timelines, waitlists, or water-main-coordinated replacements.

streamwood.water_system: Village of Streamwood operates its own distribution system (water mains, four elevated tanks, two ground storage tanks, four emergency wells); drinking water is Lake Michigan water purchased from the Northwest Suburban Municipal Joint Action Water Agency (JAWA), which owns and operates the high-service pumping station in town.
streamwood.program_name: not named (no program — Village reports no lead service lines)
streamwood.cost_coverage: not published (the Village reports no known lead service lines per its completed service-line inventory, so no lead-replacement cost-coverage program is posted; for general private water/sewer service-line repairs the homeowner is responsible for their portion, with optional paid Service Line Warranties of America (SLWA, a HomeServe USA company) warranty plans offered to Streamwood homeowners)
streamwood.homeowner_cost: not published (no lead replacement program exists; for general private service-line repairs the homeowner is responsible, with an optional Service Line Warranties of America/HomeServe warranty program offered)
streamwood.how_to_check_line: not published — no inventory map/portal is posted; the Village states it completed a service line inventory finding no lead services. Public Works can be reached at (630) 736-3850 (business hours) per the water quality page.
streamwood.how_to_apply: not published (no lead replacement program to apply to)
streamwood.notes: Streamwood's official Water Quality and Conservation page (streamwood.org, snapshot verified April 2026 via archive because the live site blocks automated fetches with 403) states the Village inventoried its water service lines and found NO lead services in its system — so no LSLRNA replacement program is needed or offered. Water source: Lake Michigan via JAWA; the Village publishes an annual Consumer Confidence Report / Water Quality Report. Related resident programs (not lead-specific): optional SLWA/HomeServe water and sewer line warranty plans, and a sewer back-up cost-share where the Village reimburses 50% up to $5,000 for overhead sewer installation (check valves also covered). Content read from web.archive.org snapshots (20260419 and 20260210) of the official streamwood.org pages, since streamwood.org returned HTTP 403 to direct and unblocked fetches.

vernon-hills.water_system: Lake County Public Works (LCPW) — the Village of Vernon Hills has no water utility of its own. Vernon Hills' official Utilities page lists "Lake County Public Works" (847-377-7500) as the water/sewer provider. LCPW owns and operates the "Vernon Hills Water System" (~28,500-30,000 residents, 118 miles of main), with Lake Michigan water purchased from the Central Lake County Joint Action Water Agency (CLCJAWA), treated at the Paul M. Neal facility in Lake Bluff. So Lake County's (not the Village's) lead service line program applies.
vernon-hills.program_name: not named (LCPW "lead service line inventory" and state-required "lead service line replacement plan")
vernon-hills.cost_coverage: not published. LCPW's official "Lead and Your Water Supply" page states only: "Illinois State law requires all Illinois utilities to develop and submit lead service line replacement plans. LCPW has developed this initial plan (PDF) to comply with the law and the federal Lead and Copper Rule Revision. It's being updated annually and will be resubmitted to the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency until the final plan and inventory are submitted in April 2027." No statement found on who pays for public vs. private portions.
vernon-hills.how_to_check_line: Official interactive map: LCPW publishes "an interactive map that shows the locations and materials of water service lines that connect to LCPW's water system" (linked from lakecountyil.gov/3668; ArcGIS viewer at lakecountyil.maps.arcgis.com, app id 2e379249dc564523afcc2670d15f7188). Residents can also self-check via lakecountyil.gov/ServiceLineCheck — LCPW "encourages all customers who own structures built in 1986 or earlier to check the water service line in their homes" using the county's identification guide — and submit results via the Water Service Line Self-Identification Form (Survey123).
vernon-hills.how_to_apply: not published (no application process stated). Contact: Lake County Public Works, publicworks@lakecountyil.gov, 847-377-7500.
vernon-hills.notes: LCPW's initial replacement plan is being updated and resubmitted to Illinois EPA annually until the final plan and inventory are due in April 2027 — the program is currently in the inventory/planning phase; official pages describe no active homeowner-facing replacement scheduling, funding, or waitlist. The county's GovDelivery bulletin notes the self-ID form is only for LCPW customers (which Vernon Hills residents are); those on village-run systems or private wells should not submit. Vernon Hills-specific water quality data is published in LCPW's annual "Vernon Hills Water Service Area" Consumer Confidence Report (lakecountyil.gov DocumentCenter). lakecountyil.gov blocks direct fetches (Cloudflare); page content above was obtained via search-index extraction of the official pages plus the county's official GovDelivery bulletin.

western-springs.water_system: Own municipal system — the Village pumps water from its own local wells (one emergency shallow well, three deep wells) to a reverse-osmosis treatment plant at 614 Hillgrove, serving 4,400+ customers
western-springs.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Project (village-side, IEPA-funded) plus the Lead Service Line Replacement (LSLR) Cost Share Program (private side)
western-springs.cost_coverage: Under the Cost Share Program (detached single-family homes with a lead service line only), the homeowner arranges and pays for the private-side replacement and can "be reimbursed up to $5,000 to replace their private service"; the village pages do not explicitly describe the payment timing, and costs beyond $5,000 are not reimbursed. Reimbursement is conditional: owners are ineligible if they have unpaid taxes, water bills, Village fees or other Village debt, unpaid Village liens, or uncorrected notified code violations, and each owner may receive the reimbursement only once. The application must include three quotes from licensed Illinois plumbers, and a building permit is required before work proceeds. For homes replaced in the village's annual IEPA-loan-funded phases, the official pages do not publish a homeowner cost — the cost split for village-scheduled replacements is not published beyond Phase 1 being described as "wholly funded" by the IEPA LSLR Loan.
western-springs.homeowner_cost: Under the Cost Share Program the homeowner arranges and pays for the private-side replacement and can "be reimbursed up to $5,000 to replace their private service" (the official pages do not describe payment timing; costs beyond $5,000 are not reimbursed). Reimbursement is conditional: owners must be in good standing with the Village (no unpaid taxes, water bills, Village fees or debt, no unpaid Village liens, no uncorrected notified code violations), may receive the reimbursement only once, and must apply with three quotes from licensed Illinois plumbers and obtain a building permit before work proceeds. For homes picked up in the village's annual IEPA-loan-funded phases, the official pages do not publish a homeowner cost — cost split for village-scheduled replacements is not published beyond "wholly funded" Phase 1.
western-springs.how_to_check_line: Official Lead Service Line Inventory — an interactive ArcGIS map portal linked from the village LSLR Project page (wsprings.com/538) — lets residents look up their property's service line material
western-springs.how_to_apply: Cost Share: submit the "Lead Service Line Replacement Cost Share Application" to LSLRcostshare@wsprings.com with three quotes from licensed Illinois plumbers; after village verifies good standing and approves, submit a Building Permit Application to the same email. Village Hall: 740 Hillgrove Ave, 708-246-1800. For the village replacement project: contact Water Plant Superintendent Ronald Derengowski or Lead Water Plant Operator Jason Muncy (emails on wsprings.com/538), or sign up for the LSLR NewsFlash.
western-springs.notes: 15-year replacement plan (Fall 2024–2037), ~7% of lead lines per year per the Illinois LSLR and Notification Act; the village updates the plan annually (2025 and 2026 LSLR Plans posted as PDFs). The village states it cannot currently give residents a specific replacement date. Cost Share eligibility requires good standing with the village (no unpaid taxes/water bills/liens/fees, no uncorrected code violations) and is one-time per applicant; no application deadline published. Official pages fetched do not mention coordination with water-main projects.

wheeling.water_system: Village of Wheeling operates its own community water supply (State Water System ID IL0314970); it purchases Lake Michigan surface water through the Northwest Water Commission (NWWC), which receives water treated and pumped by the City of Evanston, delivered to Wheeling's three receiving stations.
wheeling.cost_coverage: Official pages state no active program because the work is done: per the Village's Annual Water Quality Report (Jan 1–Dec 31, 2025), "The Village of Wheeling is responsible for providing high quality drinking water and removing lead pipes" and "All lead service lines have been removed in the Village of Wheeling." Cost-coverage terms of the past replacement effort are not published on official pages.
wheeling.homeowner_cost: not published (no replacement program remains — the Village states all lead service lines have been removed)
wheeling.how_to_check_line: Per the Annual Water Quality Report: "The most recent service line material inventory is available on the Village website under Utility Division/Related Documents" (wheelingil.gov/435 — 'IEPA 2024 Lead Service Line Inventory Template' and 'IEPA 2023 Lead Service Line Listing' documents). Residents can also obtain a copy of the service line inventory or lead tap sampling data from Utility Superintendent Jeff Wolfgram, 847-279-6928, jwolfgram@wheelingil.gov.
wheeling.how_to_apply: not published (no application process exists; contact for lead/water questions is Utility Superintendent Jeff Wolfgram, 847-279-6928, jwolfgram@wheelingil.gov)
wheeling.notes: Wheeling is a completed-replacement community: the official report states twice that all lead service lines have been removed ("Our Community Water Supply has developed a service line material inventory. All lead service lines have been removed."). Lead 90th percentile was 1.5 ppb (2023 sampling), well under the 15 ppb action level, 0 sites exceeding. The report still advises residents that lead can come from private home plumbing and offers water testing via the Utility Superintendent. Non-official news coverage (WaterWorld/Daily Herald) describes the 2019-2021 project that replaced ~110 lead lines with copper using an IEPA low-interest loan with partial forgiveness plus an NWWC grant, but those cost details do not appear on official Village pages.

willow-springs.water_system: Willow Springs does not run its own water utility. The village's official site states: "Water service and billing is through JUSTICE-WILLOW SPRINGS WATER COMMISSION" (JWSWC, 7000 S. Archer Rd, Justice, IL 60458, 708-458-7010, jwswc.org), a joint commission serving Justice and Willow Springs.
willow-springs.cost_coverage: not published — neither the Village of Willow Springs site nor JWSWC publishes a lead service line replacement program or any cost-coverage policy. JWSWC's published 2024 IEPA service line material inventory classifies every serviced address as Non-Lead (NL), so no replacement program appears to be needed or offered.
willow-springs.how_to_check_line: JWSWC posts its full IEPA service line material inventory as a downloadable PDF on its Water Quality Reports page (jwswc.org/water-quality-reports/, "Lead Service Line Inventory — View Results"), listing every serviced address with utility-side and customer-side material and an entire-service-line classification. In the 2024 Final Material Inventory, all ~2,707 rows (about 2,166 Willow Springs addresses) are classified "NL" (Non-Lead); no Lead (L), Galvanized Requiring Replacement (GRR), or Unknown (U) classifications appear. Residents can also call JWSWC at (708) 458-7010.
willow-springs.how_to_apply: not published — no application process exists because no replacement program is published; contact JWSWC at (708) 458-7010 or 7000 Archer Rd, Justice, IL 60458 for service line questions.
willow-springs.notes: JWSWC's inventory reporting zero lead/GRR/unknown service lines means the Illinois LSLR Act's replacement mandate effectively does not generate a program here. JWSWC also posts 2024 Lead & Copper sampling results (jwswc.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/2024-Lead-and-Copper.pdf) and annual water quality reports 2019-2026. JWSWC runs an ongoing water main replacement capital program (project pages on jwswc.org/projects/); search-cached JWSWC project pages stated the Commission "has no knowledge of any lead service pipes or leaded joints in the mains" within project limits and that during main replacement new service lines are installed in the public right of way and connected to existing private lines at about the property line — those two specific project pages returned 404 when fetched directly, so treat that quote as from a cached official page. The Village of Willow Springs website itself publishes nothing on lead service lines.

wilmette.water_system: Village of Wilmette operates its own community water supply (IEPA facility ID IL0313300 per the Village's draft Lead Service Line Replacement Plan); the Village's dedicated lead program site is wilmettelead.info, linked from wilmette.gov
wilmette.program_name: Lead Service Line Replacement Policy (adopted by the Village Board September 10, 2024); referred to as the "Village-wide lead service replacement program"
wilmette.cost_coverage: $0 if replaced through the Village-wide lead service replacement program, which the official Village handout (dated 9/26/2024) states "is 100% Village-funded" — note the program is still being rolled out (final replacement plan due to IEPA by April 15, 2027; ~2,200 lead lines to be replaced by 2044), so a wait may be involved; full cost to the homeowner for elective replacement or replacement triggered by a home upgrade (home addition, demolition for a new home, or added fixtures requiring a service upgrade); for a damaged/leaking lead or galvanized service or inoperative main service valve, "The Village may share in some of the costs" (share amount not published — contact Public Works, 847-853-7500)
wilmette.homeowner_cost: $0 if replaced through the Village-wide program ("100% Village-funded"); full cost if the homeowner replaces electively or due to a home upgrade/new construction; cost may be shared by the Village for damaged/leaking lead or galvanized services (amount not published)
wilmette.how_to_check_line: Wilmette Lead Service Inventory Public Dashboard (interactive ArcGIS map linked from wilmettelead.info/inventory/); residents can also self-check (scratch/magnet test), submit a photo, complete the Village's Water Service Line Survey online, or request an in-home inspection from Engineering and Public Works at 847-853-7500 or pubworks@wilmette.com
wilmette.how_to_apply: Contact Wilmette Public Works / Engineering and Public Works Department at 847-853-7500 (7 AM-3 PM Mon-Fri) or pubworks@wilmette.com; the official pages do not publish a formal application form for the program
wilmette.notes: Wilmette has approximately 2,200 lead service lines that must be replaced by 2044 under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act (the 9/26/2024 Village handout says 2044; the FAQ page cites a state-mandated deadline of 2042). Draft LSLR plan submitted to IEPA in 2024; final plan due 2027 (FAQ cites April 15, 2027 target). Program replacements are being coordinated with Village capital work; the Village has authorized borrowing from the IEPA Public Water Supply Loan Program for replacements (per search summary of Village board materials). Over 300 service lines still have unknown material; properties with confirmed lead lines are notified annually by mail. The official handout advises homeowners considering elective replacement to wait for the 100% Village-funded program. No waitlist, per-property schedule, or homeowner financial-assistance/loan program is published on the official pages.

winnetka.water_system: Village of Winnetka's own municipal utility — the Winnetka Water & Electric Department operates the potable water system (4,494 service connections; approximately one-third of service lines are lead and/or partially lead per the Village's official notification)
winnetka.program_name: Voluntary Lead Service Line Replacement Program (plus Village-funded public-side replacement during water main capital improvement projects and a cost-share for emergent/leaking line replacements)
winnetka.cost_coverage: Per the Village's March 7, 2024 lead water service notification (stated for the 2024 program year; "continuation of this program in forthcoming years is subject to budget consideration" — confirm current terms with the Water & Electric Office, 847-716-3558): three scenarios. (1) Leaking lead service line: "For 2024, the Village will cover 50% of the replacement cost, up to $5,000, for the replacement of a leaking lead water service line" — intended to assist with contractor costs, permitting fees, water meter replacement, and tapping fees; customers must secure quotes from at least two licensed, bonded plumbers. (2) Water main projects: "As part of the water main capital improvement project, the Village will fund replacement of the lead service line from the water main to the property line," and "the Village will reimburse a customer up to 50% of the cost, not to exceed $5,000, for the replacement of their lead service line from the property line into the house" (includes new water meter and inspection); customers may use the Village's contractor or their own licensed contractor. (3) Voluntary program (2024): "The Village will extend reimbursement up to 50% of the cost, not to exceed $5,000, for the replacement of the lead service line from the water main into the house"; eligible costs include the contractor's installation cost plus Village tapping fee, inspection fee, and new water meter; requires two plumber quotes. However, for 2024 this voluntary program was limited to the first eighty residences on the 2023 waiting list, with others added to a waiting list served only "if additional funding becomes available." Not eligible if the replacement is part of new house construction or a building addition. Note: the Village's current Lead Service Line Replacement page and water FAQ do not describe any reimbursement program — the FAQ states "replacement of the lead water service is the responsibility of the customer" — so these cost-share terms are documented only in the 2024 notification and may no longer be in effect. Homeowner cost: homeowner pays the remainder after the Village's 50% reimbursement capped at $5,000 (private-side replacement in main projects; full line water-main-to-house in the voluntary and leak scenarios, minus the reimbursement). In water main projects the Village fully funds the water-main-to-property-line segment. Customers using the Village's contractor must pay their portion within 30 days of completed installation; payment arrangements can be discussed with the Village. Homeowners refusing replacement must sign a waiver and bear sole responsibility for lead mitigation.
winnetka.homeowner_cost: Per the Village's March 7, 2024 notification, stated for the 2024 program year ("continuation of this program in forthcoming years is subject to budget consideration"; the Village's current LSLR page and FAQ describe no reimbursement program — confirm current terms with the Water & Electric Office, 847-716-3558): homeowner pays the remainder after the Village's 50% reimbursement capped at $5,000 (private-side replacement in main projects; full line water-main-to-house in the voluntary and leak scenarios, minus the reimbursement); quotes from at least two licensed, bonded plumbers are required, and the 2024 voluntary program was limited to the first eighty residences on the 2023 waiting list, with others served only "if additional funding becomes available." In water main projects the Village fully funds the water-main-to-property-line segment. Customers using the Village's contractor must pay their portion within 30 days of completed installation; payment arrangements can be discussed with the Village. Homeowners refusing replacement must sign a waiver and bear sole responsibility for lead mitigation.
winnetka.how_to_check_line: The Village publishes an address-level service line material inventory (updated annually by April 15 per 415 ILCS 5/17.12), available as "Water Service Data by Address" in the Village website's Document Center; the FAQ also describes self-checking via a scratch test (lead shows bright silver) or confirmation by a certified plumber or the Water & Electric Department.
winnetka.how_to_apply: For the Voluntary LSL Replacement Program: contact the Permit Coordinator in the Community Development Department at Village Hall, 510 Green Bay Road, Winnetka, or call 847-716-3520, and ask to be added to the waiting list. Applicants must secure quotes from at least two licensed, bonded plumbers for a new 1 1/2-inch copper line. General questions: Water & Electric Office, 847-716-3558 or LSL@Winnetka.org.
winnetka.notes: Per the official notification, all Winnetka lead water services must be replaced by 2038 under the Illinois Lead Service Line Replacement and Notification Act; partial replacements are prohibited (leaking lines must be fully replaced within 30 days of an emergency repair). The voluntary program operates on a waiting list — for 2024 it served the first eighty residences from the 2023 waitlist, and "continuation of this program in forthcoming years is subject to budget consideration." Replacements are also driven by annual water main capital improvement project areas (e.g., 2024: Cherry St and Spruce St, Locust to Birch), where affected lead-service properties are required to fully replace their lines and receive a Village cost estimate for the private-side work. The program page notes a final replacement plan is due to IEPA April 15, 2027. No loan program is published; the Village offers payment arrangements for its contractor's private-side charges.
